Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 122–123:

Explanation of the words:

Israel (Isra'il): the epithet of Ya'qub, son of Ishaq, son of Ibrahim, peace be upon them.

Banu Isra'il (Children of Israel): they are the Jews.

Al-'alamin (the worlds): the people who existed in their time, absolutely.

La tajzi (will not avail): will not suffice and will not benefit.

Al-'adl (ransom): the ransom.

Shafa'ah (intercession): the mediation of someone.

The meaning of the two verses:

The Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, admonishes the Jews, addressing them by their most honourable titles, and commands them to remember His blessings upon them, which are many, and to remember that He preferred them over the worlds of their time. By remembering the blessings is meant giving thanks for them. Thus, He, exalted is He, in reality commands them to give thanks for His blessings, and that is by believing in Him and His Messenger and entering His true religion (Islam).

He also commands them to guard against the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, on which no soul will avail another soul in anything, no ransom will be accepted from it, and no intercession will benefit it. This is the state of the disbeliever and the polytheist, for no intercession will reach the disbeliever or the polytheist, and they will have no helper to repel the punishment from them. Guarding against the punishment of the Day of Resurrection is achieved by faith in Allah and His Messenger and righteous deeds, after abandoning disbelief and sins.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The obligation of remembering Allah's blessings upon the servant, so that he finds in that a psychological impetus to give thanks for them, since the ultimate purpose of remembrance is thanksgiving.

2- The obligation of guarding against the punishment of the Day of Resurrection through faith and righteous deeds, after abandoning shirk and disobedience.

3- The impossibility of ransom on the Day of Resurrection, and the unavailability of any intercessor who would intercede for one who died in shirk, either to bring him out of the Fire or to lighten the punishment for him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 124:

Explanation of the words:

ibtala (tested): He examined him by assigning him burdensome matters.

bi-kalimat (with words): including commands and prohibitions.

atammahunna (he fulfilled them): he carried them out and performed them in the most complete manner.

imaman (an imam): a good example to be followed in goodness and perfection.

al-zalimin (the wrongdoers): the disbelievers, the polytheists, and the corrupt who transgress against people.

Meaning of the noble verse:

After the lengthy debate that the Messenger (ﷺ) had with the two groups of the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, as well as the polytheists, in the verses preceding this one, Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger to mention His testing of His prophet and intimate friend Ibrahim (peace be upon him) with the duties and prohibitions with which He charged him. He carried them out in the best manner, so Allah bestowed upon him the greatest of favours, which is that He made him an imam for mankind. Among the most prominent of those duties were his standing against the idol-worshippers, smashing their idols, emigrating from their homeland, his resolve to slaughter his son Isma'il as a sacrifice to Allah, building the House, performing its pilgrimage, and calling to it. These are what earned him the imamate over all people. In this there is a rebuke to the three groups: the Arab polytheists, the Jews and the Christians, for all of them claim to be affiliated to Ibrahim and to follow his creed. Yet here is Ibrahim, a monotheist, while they are polytheists; just, while they are wrongdoers; one who follows the divine revelation, while they disbelieve in it and deny its bearer. The verse also shows Ibrahim's desire that the imamate remain among his descendants, which was a righteous desire, so Allah granted it to his descendants as he wished. Allah excepted the wrongdoers, for they do not deserve it. It is only for people of goodness, justice and mercy; it is not for tyrants, cruel ones, or stubborn wrongdoers.

Guidance from the verse:

Among the guidance of the verse:

1- Imamate is not attained except through true certainty and patience in following the path of the rightly guided.

2- The legitimacy of appointing a successor, on condition that one appoints only someone who is at the highest level of faith, knowledge, action, justice and patience.

3- Carrying out the legal duties, in word and deed, qualifies a person to be a good example for people.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 125–126:

Explanation of the words:

Al-bayt (the House): the Ka'bah, which is the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram) in Makkah al-Mukarramah.

Mathabah: a place to which people return repeatedly; the 'umar (those performing 'umrah) and the pilgrims return to it.

Amnan: a secure place in which everyone who enters it is safe.

Maqam Ibrahim (the Station of Ibrahim): the stone on which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) stood while he was building the House. When the building rose high, Ibrahim needed a high stone to climb upon in order to continue building the walls, so this stone was brought and he stood on it; hence it was named the Station of Ibrahim.

Musalla: a place where one prays, or at it, or facing it.

'Ahidna: We enjoined and commanded.

Tathhir al-bayt (purifying the House): cleansing it from physical impurities such as blood and urine, and from spiritual impurities such as polytheism, innovations and corruptions.

Idtarrahu: compelled him, forcing him unwillingly toward the punishment.

Meaning of the two verses:

The context continues to remind both the polytheists and the People of the Book of the father of the prophets and imam of the monotheists, Ibrahim (peace be upon him), with his good and praiseworthy virtues and his great acts of faith, so that thereby the falsehood of the claim of both the People of the Book and the polytheists to descent from Ibrahim, a false and baseless claim, becomes manifest, since he was a monotheist while they are polytheists, and he was a believer while they are disbelievers. Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (ﷺ): Mention to them how We made the House a mathabah for the people, to which they return in every age as pilgrims and visitors, and a place of security forever: whoever enters it is secure for his self, his property and his honour. And We said to those who perform Hajj to the House or 'umrah: take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer. So it was the sunnah of whoever circumambulates the House to pray two rak'ahs behind the Station, as We had enjoined upon Ibrahim and his son Isma'il before: to purify the House from every impurity, spiritual, such as idols and the worship of other than Allah the Exalted, or physical, such as filth and dirt, blood or urine, so that those who circumambulate, those who remain in devotion, and those who pray may perform these acts of worship without any harm befalling them or troubling them.

This is what the verse [125] contained. As for the second [126], it contained the command of Allah the Exalted to His Messenger to mention the supplication of Ibrahim to his Lord that He make Makkah a secure land, where whoever enters is safe for his self, his property and his honour, and that He provide its people and inhabitants who believe with fruits; and that Allah answered Ibrahim's supplication. However, the disbelievers are not deprived of provision in this world, but they are deprived of Paradise in the Hereafter, where the Exalted compels them, unwillingly, to the severe punishment of the Fire. And wretched is this destination to which they come — which is the Fire.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Allah the Exalted's favour in making the House a mathabah and a place of security for people, which obliges every believer to praise Allah.

2- The sunnah of praying two rak'ahs behind the Station for whoever circumambulates the House.

3- The obligation to protect the House and the Sacred Mosque from any harm that may befall whoever is present in it, whether circumambulating, remaining in devotion, standing, bowing or prostrating.

4- The blessing of Ibrahim's supplication for the people of Makkah, and Allah the Exalted's answering of his supplication; so to Allah belongs all praise and favour.

5- The disbeliever is not deprived of provision because of his disbelief; rather he has the right to life, unless he wages war, in which case he is killed or submits.

6- The destiny of one who dies a disbeliever is the Fire, without doubt, and dying within the Sacred Precinct does not avail the disbeliever anything.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 127–129:

Explanation of the words:

{Wa-idh} (and when): an adverb referring to a past time, and it is connected to an implied verb, its meaning being: "Remember the time when such-and-such happened."

{Al-qawa'id} (the foundations): the plural of qa'idah, meaning the base upon which a wall is built, such as its foundation and the like.

{Al-bayt} (the House): the Ka'bah, may Allah protect and purify it.

{Innaka anta as-Sami' al-'Alim} (Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing): this sentence is a means (wasilah) by which Ibrahim and his son sought to have their supplication accepted.

{Muslimayn} (submitting to You): submitting to You, humbled before Your command and Your prohibition, content with Your judgment, worshipping You.

{Arina manasikana} (Show us our rites): teach us how to perform the Hajj to Your House, as acts of devotion (tansuk) and worship (ta'abbud) to You.

{Tub 'alayna} (Accept our repentance): grant us success in repentance when we slip, and accept it from us.

{Wa-ub'ath fihim rasulan} (And send among them a messenger): this supplication is the response of Allah the Exalted, and Muhammad ﷺ is what the two of them asked for.

{Al-Kitab} (the Book): the Qur'an.

{Al-Hikmah} (the Wisdom): the Sunnah, the secrets of the Shari'ah, and correctness in all matters.

{Yuzakkihim} (purify them): purify their souls, perfect their minds, and refine their character, by teaching them the Book and the Wisdom, and by clarifying for them the various kinds of acts of obedience.

{Al-'Aziz al-Hakim} (the Mighty, the Wise): Al-'Aziz is the Overpowering who cannot be overpowered. Al-Hakim is the One who is wise in His creation and His management, placing everything in its proper place.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to mention the virtues of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, which reveal his lofty station in perfect faith and obedience, and his great eagerness for good and mercy. The three verses include the mention of Ibrahim and Isma'il as they build the House by raising its foundations, while they call upon Allah the Exalted that He accept their deed from them, seeking a means to Him through His names and attributes: {Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing}.

They also ask Him, Mighty and Majestic, to make them submissive to Him, and to make from their offspring a community submitting to Him, believing in Him, affirming His oneness, obedient to His command and prohibition, and obedient; and to teach them the rites of the Hajj to His Ancient House so that they may perform it with knowledge, and to accept their repentance. They also asked Him, Mighty and Majestic, to send among their offspring a messenger from among them who recites to them the verses of Allah, teaches them the Book and the Wisdom, and purifies them through faith, righteous deeds, beautiful qualities and good characteristics.

Allah the Exalted responded to their supplication and sent among their offspring, from the sons of Isma'il, the leader of the Muslims and the commander of the bright-faced ones, our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. And he ﷺ confirmed this by his saying: "I am the answer to the supplication of my father Ibrahim, and the glad tidings of 'Isa... peace be upon them all." 

Guidance from the verses:

1- The virtue of contributing oneself to the building of mosques.

2- The believer who is insightful in his religion does good while fearing that it will not be accepted from him, so he asks Allah the Exalted and seeks a means to Him through His names and attributes that He accept it from him.

3- The legitimacy of asking Allah for oneself and for one's offspring to remain steadfast upon Islam until death.

4- The obligation of learning the rites of Hajj and 'Umrah for whoever intends to perform Hajj or 'Umrah.

5- The obligation of seeking the purification of the soul through faith and righteous deeds, and the refinement of character through knowledge and wisdom.

6- The legitimacy of seeking a means to Allah in having supplication accepted, namely through His names and attributes, not through the right of so-and-so or the status of so-and-so, as is the practice of the innovators and the misguided. In these three verses, Ibrahim and Isma'il sought a means through the following phrases:

1- {Innaka anta as-Sami' al-'Alim}.

2- {Innaka anta at-Tawwab ar-Rahim}.

3- {Innaka anta al-'Aziz al-Hakim}.

2- The believer who is insightful in his religion does good while fearing that it will not be accepted from him, so he asks Allah the Exalted and seeks a means to Him through His names and attributes that He accept it from him.

3- The legitimacy of asking Allah for oneself and for one's offspring to remain steadfast upon Islam until death.

4- The obligation of learning the rites of Hajj and 'Umrah for whoever intends to perform Hajj or 'Umrah.

5- The obligation of seeking the purification of the soul through faith and righteous deeds, and the refinement of character through knowledge and wisdom.

6- The legitimacy of seeking a means to Allah in having supplication accepted, namely through His names and attributes, not through the right of so-and-so or the status of so-and-so, as is the practice of the innovators and the misguided. 1- {Innaka anta as-Sami' al-'Alim}.

2- {Innaka anta at-Tawwab ar-Rahim}.

3- {Innaka anta al-'Aziz al-Hakim}.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 127–129:

Explanation of the words:

{Wa-idh} (and when): an adverb referring to a past time, and it is connected to an implied verb, its meaning being: "Remember the time when such-and-such happened."

{Al-qawa'id} (the foundations): the plural of qa'idah, meaning the base upon which a wall is built, such as its foundation and the like.

{Al-bayt} (the House): the Ka'bah, may Allah protect and purify it.

{Innaka anta as-Sami' al-'Alim} (Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing): this sentence is a means (wasilah) by which Ibrahim and his son sought to have their supplication accepted.

{Muslimayn} (submitting to You): submitting to You, humbled before Your command and Your prohibition, content with Your judgment, worshipping You.

{Arina manasikana} (Show us our rites): teach us how to perform the Hajj to Your House, as acts of devotion (tansuk) and worship (ta'abbud) to You.

{Tub 'alayna} (Accept our repentance): grant us success in repentance when we slip, and accept it from us.

{Wa-ub'ath fihim rasulan} (And send among them a messenger): this supplication is the response of Allah the Exalted, and Muhammad ﷺ is what the two of them asked for.

{Al-Kitab} (the Book): the Qur'an.

{Al-Hikmah} (the Wisdom): the Sunnah, the secrets of the Shari'ah, and correctness in all matters.

{Yuzakkihim} (purify them): purify their souls, perfect their minds, and refine their character, by teaching them the Book and the Wisdom, and by clarifying for them the various kinds of acts of obedience.

{Al-'Aziz al-Hakim} (the Mighty, the Wise): Al-'Aziz is the Overpowering who cannot be overpowered. Al-Hakim is the One who is wise in His creation and His management, placing everything in its proper place.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to mention the virtues of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, which reveal his lofty station in perfect faith and obedience, and his great eagerness for good and mercy. The three verses include the mention of Ibrahim and Isma'il as they build the House by raising its foundations, while they call upon Allah the Exalted that He accept their deed from them, seeking a means to Him through His names and attributes: {Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing}.

They also ask Him, Mighty and Majestic, to make them submissive to Him, and to make from their offspring a community submitting to Him, believing in Him, affirming His oneness, obedient to His command and prohibition, and obedient; and to teach them the rites of the Hajj to His Ancient House so that they may perform it with knowledge, and to accept their repentance. They also asked Him, Mighty and Majestic, to send among their offspring a messenger from among them who recites to them the verses of Allah, teaches them the Book and the Wisdom, and purifies them through faith, righteous deeds, beautiful qualities and good characteristics.

Allah the Exalted responded to their supplication and sent among their offspring, from the sons of Isma'il, the leader of the Muslims and the commander of the bright-faced ones, our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. And he ﷺ confirmed this by his saying: "I am the answer to the supplication of my father Ibrahim, and the glad tidings of 'Isa... peace be upon them all."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafsir) on surah 2, verses 130–134:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa man yarghabu 'an millati Ibrahim* (And who would turn away from the religion of Ibrahim): *al-raghba 'an al-shay'* (turning away from a thing) is not loving it and abandoning the seeking of it. The *millat Ibrahim* (the religion/creed of Ibrahim) is the worship of Allah alone in the manner He has prescribed for His servants.

*Illa man safiha nafsahu* (Except one who has foolishly belittled himself): No one turns away from the religion of Ibrahim, which is the religion of Islam, except a servant who has ignorantly disregarded his own worth, humiliating and degrading himself by abandoning the path of his honour, perfection and happiness, which is Islam.

*Istafaynahu* (We chose him): We selected him for Our message and for conveying Our word. For this reason We elevated his station and exalted his rank.

*Aslim* (Submit): Obey Our command and prohibition; worship Us alone and do not turn to anyone else.

*Isţafa lakumu al-din* (He has chosen for you this religion): He chose for you the religion of Islam and was pleased with it for you, so do not die except as Muslims.

*Ya'qub* (Jacob): He is Israel, son of Isaac, son of Ibrahim, and his sons are Yusuf and his brothers.

*Ummatun qad khalat* (A community that has passed away): a group whose affair is one. *Khalat*: passed on to the Hereafter.

*Laha ma kasabat* (For it is what it earned): the reward of the good it earned.

*Wa lakum ma kasabtum* (And for you is what you have earned): whether good or otherwise.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in the preceding verses the upright and sound positions of Ibrahim in creed, sincerity, righteous action, truthfulness and fidelity, thereby clarifying the correct religion that Ibrahim held, He said: ﴿And who would turn away from the religion of Ibrahim?﴾, that upright, clear and easy creed. No one turns away from it except a servant who has ignorantly disregarded his own worth and did not recognise its rights of purity, clarity, perfection and happiness. Within this statement, Allah mentioned His favour upon Ibrahim and what He bestowed upon him of choosing in this world and happiness in the Hereafter, among the righteous.

In the second verse [131], Allah mentions that this choosing was completed for Ibrahim when he answered his Lord's command to submit, for he submitted without hesitation. In the third verse [132], Allah mentions the establishment of proof against the polytheists and the People of the Book together, for the religion of Islam, founded on monotheism, is what Ibrahim enjoined upon his sons, just as Jacob enjoined it upon his sons, saying to them: "Do not die except in Islam." So where is Arab idolatry, Judaism and Christianity from the religion of Ibrahim? Let the intelligent return to their right guidance.

In the fourth verse [133], Allah rebukes the Jews who falsely and baselessly said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Do you not know that Jacob enjoined his sons with Judaism?" Allah said: ﴿Or were you witnesses﴾, meaning, were you present when death came to Jacob and he said to his sons, questioning them: "What will you worship after me?" They answered him with one voice: ﴿We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq, one God, and to Him we are Muslims.﴾ If they say they were present, they have lied, been astonished and been cursed; and if they say they were not present, their claim that Jacob enjoined his sons with Judaism is refuted, and it is established that he enjoined them with Islam, not Judaism.

In the last verse [134], Allah ends the vain disputation of the Jews, saying to them: ﴿That is a community that has passed away﴾, meaning Ibrahim and his descendants, ﴿for it is what it earned of faith and righteous deeds, and for you, O assembly of Jews, is what you have earned of disbelief and sins. And you will not be asked about the deeds of others on the Day of Resurrection; rather you will be asked about your own deeds and be recompensed for them.* So abandon disputation and attend to what benefits you in your Hereafter, which is sound faith and righteous action, and this will not be complete for you except through Islam, so submit.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Only a foolish person who does not know his own worth turns away from Islam by abandoning it or seeking other religions.

2- Islam is the religion of all humanity, and whatever is other than it is innovated, false religions.

3- It is recommended for a sick person to make a bequest in which he enjoins his sons and the rest of his family to Islam until death.

4- The Jews lied and slandered, and the one who said "the Jews are a people of slander" spoke truly.

5- It is good for a person to abandon pride in the nobility and righteousness of those who came before, and to turn to himself by purifying and cleansing it.

6- It is Allah's way in creation that a person is recompensed for his deeds, and is not asked about the deeds of another.

7- The term "father" is applied to an uncle by way of preponderance and honour.

**Explanation of the Words:**

*Atuhajjunana fi Allah* (Do you dispute with us about God?): Do you argue with us about His religion and faith in Him and His Messenger? The interrogative form is one of denunciation.

*Lahu mukhlisun* (We are sincere to Him): We devote worship sincerely to Him, not associating anyone else with Him in it, while you are polytheists.

*Shahada 'indahu min Allah* (a testimony from Allah that is with them): What is meant by this testimony is what was taken from them in their Scripture concerning faith in the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ at the time of his appearance.

*Al-ghafil* (the heedless): One who does not perceive matters because he does not care about them.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

Allah commands His Messenger to denounce the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) for their disputing about Allah, the Exalted, when they claimed that they were closer to Allah than the Messenger and the believers, and said, "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved." So Allah taught His Messenger how to answer them, denouncing their false claim. He also silenced them and cut off their argument in their claim that Abraham and the prophets after him were Jews or Christians, when He said to him, "Say to them: ﴿Are you more knowing, or is Allah?﴾" If they say, "We are more knowing," they disbelieve; and if they say, "Allah is more knowing," they are left without argument, because Allah, the Exalted, has informed that they never were Jews or Christians, but were Muslims. Then Allah, the Exalted, threatened them with their greatest crime, which is their concealing the truth and their denying the attributes of the Messenger and the command to believe in him at his appearance. So He said, ﴿And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from Allah? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾

Then He repeated to them what He had disciplined them with in the previous verses, as an intensification of their discipline and reform, if they were fit for that. He informed them that clinging to the thresholds of those who have passed away, and holding to empty lineage to the ancients, is of no benefit to them and does not profit them. So let them turn to saving themselves from ignorance and disbelief through faith, Islam, and excellence (ihsan). As for those who have passed away, they are a community that has gone to what they earned, and they will be recompensed for it; and you have what you earned, and you will be recompensed for it. You will not be recompensed for the deeds of others, nor will you be questioned about them.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. The virtue of sincerity (ikhlas, sincere devotion), which is not turning to anyone other than Allah, the Exalted, when performing acts of worship.

2. Every person is recompensed for his own deeds, and is not held accountable for the deeds of another, unless he was the cause of them.

3. Judaism and Christianity are an innovation (bid'ah) invented by the Jews and the Christians.

4. Injustice varies according to the consequences that follow from it.

5. The sanctity of concealing testimony, especially a testimony from Allah, the Exalted.

6. Not relying on the lineage and ancestry of one's forefathers and grandfathers, and the obligation to turn to oneself to purify and cleanse it through correct faith and righteous deeds.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 142–143:

Explanation of the words:

Al-sufaha' (the foolish): plural of safih, a person whose intellect is weakened by blind imitation and by turning away from reflection, which results in corruption of character and bad conduct.

Ma wallahum (what turned them away): what diverted them from facing Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) to facing the Ka'bah in Makkah.

Al-qiblah (the direction of prayer): the direction a person faces, which lies before him in his prayer.

Ummatan wasatan (a middle nation): the best of every thing is its choicest part; what is meant is that the nation of Muhammad ﷺ is the best and most just of nations.

Yanqalibu 'ala 'aqibayh (turns back on his heels): returns to disbelief after faith.

La-kabirah (indeed a burden): heavy upon the soul, difficult and not bearable except with great effort; it is the shift from a familiar qiblah to a new one.

Imanakum (your faith): your prayer which you prayed facing Bayt al-Maqdis before the change to the Ka'bah.

Ra'uf rahim (Most Kind, Most Merciful): He repels harm from you and pours forth goodness upon you.

The meaning of the two verses:

Allah the Exalted informs of a matter which He knows before it occurs. The wisdom in informing of it before it happens is to lighten its effect upon the souls of the believers, since its bitter criticism loses the element of surprise, so the souls of the believers are not thrown into turmoil by it.

Thus He the Exalted says: ﴿The foolish among the people will say: What has turned them away from their qiblah which they were upon?﴾ This occurred when Allah the Exalted turned His Messenger and the believers from facing Bayt al-Maqdis in prayer to facing the Ka'bah, in fulfilment of the desire of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for that and because of the reason of testing contained in the following verse. So Allah the Exalted informed of what the foolish would say, from among the Jews, the hypocrites and the polytheists, and He taught the believers how to respond to the foolish, saying: Say: To Allah belong the East and the West; He guides whom He wills to a straight path. There is no objection to Him; He directs His servants wherever He wills, and He guides whom He wills to a straight path.

In the second verse [143], He the Exalted says: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation﴾, upright and just, meaning: just as We guided you to the best qiblah, which is the Ka'bah, the qiblah of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), We have made you the best and most just nation. Thereby We qualified you to bear witness over the nations on the Day of Resurrection when they deny that their messengers conveyed to them the messages of their Lord; and you, for this reason, are not witnessed against by the nations, but your Messenger witnesses against you. In this there is such honour and bounty as only Allah knows. Then He the Exalted mentioned the reason for the change of qiblah, saying: ﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might know who follows the Messenger﴾, so that the one who remains firm in his faith, obedience and submission to Allah and His Messenger is distinguished from the one whose soul is affected by the criticism of the foolish, so that his soul is thrown into turmoil and he goes along with the foolish and perishes by apostasy with them. Then Allah the Exalted informed that this change from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah is a burden upon the soul, except for those whom Allah has guided to knowledge of Him and knowledge of what He loves and dislikes; these therefore find no difficulty at all in moving from one act of obedience to another and from one qiblah to another, so long as their Lord has loved that and commanded it.

Finally, the Exalted reassured them concerning the rewards of their prayers which they had prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis, a period of about seventeen months, that He will not waste them for them but will recompense them in full, whether one of them died while praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis or one of them lived until he prayed toward the Ka'bah. This is a manifestation of His mercy and compassion toward His servants.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The permissibility of abrogation (naskh) in Islam: this is abrogation with a replacement, from prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis to prayer toward the Ka'bah in Makkah al-Mukarramah.

2- Rumours, fabricating crises and exaggerating matters are the conduct of the disbelievers towards the Muslims throughout life; so the believers must remain firm and not waver until falsehood is exposed, the deception is revealed and the trial comes to an end.

3- The superiority of the Muslim nation over all other nations, because it is the nation of the middle way, and moderation is its emblem.

4- The permissibility of testing the believer and of it being applied to him.

5- The validity of the prayer of one who prayed facing other than the qiblah while not knowing it, and he has its reward and is not required to repeat it, even if he prayed for months facing other than the qiblah, so long as he strove to determine the qiblah and then prayed in the direction his effort led him to.

There is no objection to Him; He directs His servants wherever He wills, and He guides whom He wills to a straight path.

In the second verse [143], He the Exalted says: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation﴾, upright and just, meaning: just as We guided you to the best qiblah, which is the Ka'bah, the qiblah of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), We have made you the best and most just nation. Thereby We qualified you to bear witness over the nations on the Day of Resurrection when they deny that their messengers conveyed to them the messages of their Lord; and you, for this reason, are not witnessed against by the nations, but your Messenger witnesses against you. In this there is such honour and bounty as only Allah knows. Then He the Exalted mentioned the reason for the change of qiblah, saying: ﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might know who follows the Messenger﴾, so that the one who remains firm in his faith, obedience and submission to Allah and His Messenger is distinguished from the one whose soul is affected by the criticism of the foolish, so that his soul is thrown into turmoil and he goes along with the foolish and perishes by apostasy with them. Then Allah the Exalted informed that this change from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah is a burden upon the soul, except for those whom Allah has guided to knowledge of Him and knowledge of what He loves and dislikes; these therefore find no difficulty at all in moving from one act of obedience to another and from one qiblah to another, so long as their Lord has loved that and commanded it.

Finally, the Exalted reassured them concerning the rewards of their prayers which they had prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis, a period of about seventeen months, that He will not waste them for them but will recompense them in full, whether one of them died while praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis or one of them lived until he prayed toward the Ka'bah. This is a manifestation of His mercy and compassion toward His servants.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The permissibility of abrogation (naskh) in Islam: this is abrogation with a replacement, from prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis to prayer toward the Ka'bah in Makkah al-Mukarramah.

2- Rumours, fabricating crises and exaggerating matters are the conduct of the disbelievers towards the Muslims throughout life; so the believers must remain firm and not waver until falsehood is exposed, the deception is revealed and the trial comes to an end.

3- The superiority of the Muslim nation over all other nations, because it is the nation of the middle way, and moderation is its emblem.

4- The permissibility of testing the believer and of it being applied to him.

5- The validity of the prayer of one who prayed facing other than the qiblah while not knowing it, and he has its reward and is not required to repeat it, even if he prayed for months facing other than the qiblah, so long as he strove to determine the qiblah and then prayed in the direction his effort led him to.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 144–147:

Explanation of the words:

"Taqallaba wajhika fi as-sama'" (Your face turning about in the sky): his repeatedly looking up towards it, waiting for the descent of revelation.

"Fa-lanuwalliyannaka qiblatan tardaha" (We shall surely turn you to a qiblah that you will be pleased with): We shall change you to the qiblah that you love, which is the Ka'bah.

"Fa-walli wajhaka shatra al-masjid" (So turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque): turn your face towards the direction of the Sacred Mosque in Makkah.

"Al-haram" (the Sacred): in the sense of the forbidden; no blood is to be shed in it and no one is to be killed in it.

"Ash-shatr" (the direction): here it means the direction, and facing the direction is achieved by facing part of the House in the Sacred Mosque, because ash-shatr linguistically means the half or the side in general.

"Annahu al-haqq min rabbihim" (That it is the truth from their Lord): that is, the change of the qiblah was stated explicitly in the earlier scriptures.

"Ayah" (a sign): proof and evidence.

"Ya'rifunahu" (they recognise him): the pronoun refers to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, meaning they know that he is the Prophet and Messenger of Allah, because of his clear and certain attributes in their books.

"Min al-mumtarin" (of those who doubt): those who are skeptical; al-imtira' is doubt and not affirming the truth.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah the Exalted informs His Messenger that He saw him turning his face towards the sky, waiting for a revelation commanding him to face the Ka'bah instead of Bayt al-Maqdis, out of his desire to differ from the Jews and his love for the qiblah of his father Ibrahim, for it was the first qiblah and the most excellent. On that basis, "So turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque." By this divine command the qiblah was changed. It is narrated that he was praying the Dhuhr prayer in the mosque of Banu Salamah, known now as Masjid al-Qiblatayn, and the Messenger and the believers prayed behind him two rak'ahs towards Bayt al-Maqdis and two rak'ahs towards the Ka'bah. And so that the qiblah would not be confined to those who were in Madinah, Allah the Exalted said: "And wherever you are" — that is, in the regions of the lands and the corners of the earth — "turn your faces towards it" — that is, towards the direction of the Sacred Mosque. As Allah the Exalted informed in this verse, the scholars of the People of the Book know that the change of the qiblah is true and that it is by the command of Allah the Exalted. As for what they produced of confusion and distortion regarding the change of the qiblah, Allah knows it and will recompense them for it, for Allah is not unaware of what they do.

In the second verse [145], Allah the Exalted informs of an established fact: that even if the Prophet ﷺ brought the Jews and Christians every sign that proves his truthfulness and the rightness of the qiblah towards the Ka'bah, they would not follow him in that and face his qiblah, just as the Christians would not pray towards Bayt al-Maqdis, the qiblah of the Jews, nor would the Jews pray towards the rising of the sun, the qiblah of the Christians. Likewise, the Prophet ﷺ and the believers would never follow the People of the Book in their qiblah after Allah has guided them to the most excellent qiblah and the one most beloved to them. Finally, Allah warns His Messenger not to follow the desires of the Jews, agreeing with them in their innovations and misguidance after the knowledge He has given him and the truth He has guided him to; and far be it from him ﷺ to do so, and had he done so, he would have been among the wrongdoers.

In the third verse [146], Allah the Exalted informs that the scholars of the People of the Book know that the Messenger is true and that what he brought is the truth, with a complete knowledge like their knowledge of their own sons. But a large group of them conceal the truth while they know that it is the truth.

In the fourth verse [147], Allah the Exalted informs His Messenger that what he is upon of the true religion is the truth sent down to him from his Lord, so he should by no means be among those who doubt.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation of facing the qiblah in prayer, and wherever the one praying is, he must face the direction of Makkah.

2- Much of the disbelief of the People of the Book was with knowledge, preferring this world over the Hereafter.

3- The prohibition of Muslims agreeing with the People of the Book on any of their religious innovations, whatever they may be.

4- The scholars of the People of the Book contemporary with the Prophet ﷺ knew that he was the promised prophet and the final prophet, yet they turned away from believing in him and following him, preferring this world over the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 148–152:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-li-kullin wijhatun huwa muwalliha: The tanwin in (kullin) indicates an omitted noun, namely: for every people of a religion, such as Islam, Judaism and Christianity, there is a qibla (direction of prayer) toward which they turn their faces in their prayers.

Al-khayrat (the good deeds): righteousness and obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

Al-hujjah (the proof): the strong evidence by which its holder prevails over the one who disputes with him.

Ni'mati (My favour): the favours of Allah are many, and the greatest of them is the favour of Islam. Its completion is by continuing legislation and acting upon it until the perfection is reached. This took place at the Farewell Pilgrimage at Arafat, when the verse was revealed: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favour upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3].

Rasulan (a Messenger): this is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the indefiniteness in it is for glorification.

Yuzakkikum (He purifies you): He cleanses you from sins, bad character and corrupt dispositions.

Al-hikmah (wisdom): the Sunnah, which is every sound statement whose soundness and benefit do not end with the passage of time.

Ash-shukr (gratitude): displaying the favour by directing it to the purpose for which Allah the Exalted bestowed it upon His servants.

Al-kufr (disbelief): denying favours, concealing them, and directing them to other than what Allah the Exalted loves.

Meaning of the verses:

After establishing that truth contained in the verse ﴿And if you were to bring to those who were given the Book every sign, they would not follow your qibla﴾ [al-Baqarah: 145], etc., namely that if the Prophet (ﷺ) brought the People of the Book every sign indicating his truthfulness regarding the matter of the qibla, they would not follow his qibla, nor is he a follower of their qibla, nor are some of them followers of the qibla of others. Neither do the Jews face the rising of the sun, nor do the Christians face Bayt al-Maqdis. Allah the Exalted informed that every nation has a qibla toward which it turns its face in prayer. So leave, O Muslims, the people of those misguided creeds, and hasten to good deeds and compete in righteous works, thanking your Lord for the blessing of guiding you to the qibla of your father Ibrahim. He, the Exalted, will gather you on the Day of Resurrection, will call you to account, and will recompense you for your deeds; indeed, He is over all things capable. Then Allah commanded His Messenger to turn his face toward the Sacred Mosque wherever he might be, whether at home or traveling, and informed him that his turning to the Ka'bah is a truth established from his Lord, the Exalted, so he should not waver in it.

This is what the two verses [148] and [149] contain. As for the verse [150], Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger and the believers to turn their faces toward the Sacred Mosque wherever they are and wherever they may be, and to remain steadfast in that, so that their enemies among the Jews and the polytheists would have no argument. The Jews say: they deny our religion yet face our qibla; and the polytheists say: they claim to be upon the creed of Ibrahim yet oppose his qibla. This applies to the moderate among them. As for the wrongdoers and the obstinate, there is no way to persuade them, for they have said in fact: he only changed to the Ka'bah out of inclination toward the religion of his forefathers, and he is about to return to it. Such people should not be cared for nor paid attention to, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿except those among them who do wrong; so do not fear them, but fear Me﴾. So remain steadfast upon your true qibla, that I may complete My favour upon you by guiding you to the best and most upright laws, and that I may prepare you for every good and perfection, just as I bestowed favour upon you by sending My Messenger, who purifies you and teaches you the Book and the wisdom, and teaches you what you did not know of the matters of religion and worldly affairs together. In the last verse [152], Allah the Exalted commanded the believers to remember Him and to thank Him, and forbade them to forget Him and disbelieve, saying: ﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you; and be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾, because in remembering Him by His names, attributes, promise and warning there are the requirements of His love and pleasure; and because in thanking Him by establishing prayer and performing all the other acts of worship there are the requirements of His mercy and grace; and because in forgetting Him and being ungrateful there is exposure to His anger, severe punishment and painful torment.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Turning away from the disputation of the obstinate, and turning to acts of obedience, competing and racing toward them, since this is more beneficial and fruitful than argument and disputes with one from whom return to the truth is not hoped for.

2- The obligation of facing the qibla in prayer, whether one is traveling or at home; except that the traveler may perform voluntary prayer wherever his mount, airplane or car turns, whether toward the qibla or otherwise.

3- The prohibition of fearing people and the obligation of fearing Allah the Exalted.

4- The obligation of thanking Allah the Exalted for His apparent and hidden favours.

5- The obligation of learning necessary knowledge so that the servant may be able to worship Allah in a way that purifies his soul.

6- The obligation of remembering Allah through tahlil, takbir and tasbih, and the obligation of thanking Him by obeying Him.

7- The prohibition of forgetting the remembrance of Allah and of denying His favours by abandoning gratitude for them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 153–157:

Explanation of the words:

Al-isti'anah (seeking aid): asking for help and for the ability to say or do something.

As-sabr (patience): restraining the self upon what is disliked and training it to bear hardships.

Ash-shu'ur (perception): awareness of a thing that leads to knowledge of it.

Al-ibtila' (trial): testing and examination to reveal the strength or weakness of the one being tested.

Al-amwal (wealth): plural of mal (wealth). It may be "speaking" wealth, namely livestock, or "silent" wealth, namely gold and silver and other things.

Al-musibah (calamity): any harm that afflicts a servant in his self, his family, or his property.

As-salawat (blessings): plural of salah. When it is from Allah here, it means forgiveness, since mercy is conjoined with it.

Wa rahmah (and mercy): rahmah is bestowal of favour, which is bringing what is pleasing and repelling what is harmful. The greatest of this is entry into Paradise after being saved from the Fire.

Al-muhtadun (the guided): guided to the path of happiness and perfection through their faith, Allah's trial of them, and their patience in that.

The meaning of the verses:

The Lord, exalted is He, called out to His believing servants, those of the religion of Islam, the Muslims, to guide them to what would be an aid to them in steadfastness upon their qibla which He chose for them, and in remembering their Lord, thanking Him, not forgetting Him, and not disbelieving. So He said: ﴿O you who have believed, seek help⦆ meaning, in what He has asked of you of steadfastness, remembrance, and gratitude, and avoiding forgetfulness and disbelief, through patience, which is training the self and compelling it to obey what Allah has commanded, and through establishing the prayer. He informed them that He is with the patient, supporting them with aid and strength, so when they are patient, Allah's help and empowerment reach them. This is what the first verse [153] contains. As for the second verse [154], it contains His prohibition to them that they say, believing that whoever is killed in the way of Allah is dead, since he is alive in the barzakh, and not dead; rather he is alive and provided for in Paradise, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The souls of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds that roam in Paradise wherever they wish, then they retire to lamps suspended beneath the Throne" (narrated by Muslim). Therefore it is not said of one who is killed in the way of Allah that he died, but rather that he was martyred; he is a martyr and alive with his Lord, with a life we do not perceive or feel, because it is separate from the life of this world. As for the third verse [155], He, exalted is He, swears to His believing servants that He will test them with some fear through His enemies and their enemies, who are the disbelievers, when they wage wars against them, and with hunger due to the siege by the enemy and other causes, and with loss of wealth such as the death of livestock through war and drought, and with loss of lives such as the death of men, and with the spoiling of crops through blights. All of this is to reveal who will be patient in their faith and in obeying their Lord by complying with His command and avoiding His prohibition, and who will not be patient and so is deprived of Allah's friendship and His reward. Then He commanded His Messenger to give good news to the patient. In the fourth verse [156] He explained the state of the patient, which is that when a calamity strikes them they say: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and to Him we return." He may afflict us with whatever He wills, since we are His possession and His servants, and to Him we return by death. Therefore there is no impatient wailing, but submission to His judgment and contentment with His decree and destiny. In the fifth verse [157], He, exalted is He, informed, giving good news to those patient ones, of the forgiveness of their sins and of mercy from their Lord, and that they are the ones guided to their happiness and perfection.

So He said: ﴿Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and those are the guided ones.﴾

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The virtue of patience, the command to it, seeking aid through patience and prayer against calamities and obligations. And in the hadith: the Prophet ﷺ, when a matter distressed him, would turn to prayer.

2- The excellence of the martyrs over others through their life with their Lord, a life more complete than the life of others in Paradise.

3- A believer may be tested with calamities in his self, family, and property so that he is patient, and his rank is raised and his station is elevated with his Lord.

4- The virtue of saying "istirja'" at the time of calamity, which is the saying: "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return." And in the Sahih, the Prophet ﷺ said: "No servant who is afflicted by a calamity and says, 'Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return. O Allah, reward me in my calamity and replace it for me with something better,' except that Allah will reward him in his calamity and replace it for him with something better" (narrated by Muslim).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 158:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Safa and al-Marwa: Al-Safa is a mountain opposite the House in its south-eastern direction, and al-Marwa is another mountain opposite al-Safa on its northern side. The distance between them is about (760) cubits.

Sha'a'ir Allah (the rites of God): the markers of His religion. It is the plural of sha'ira, which is a sign of the worship of God, the Exalted. Thus, the sa'y (running/walking) between al-Safa and al-Marwa is a sha'ira, because it indicates obedience to God, the Exalted.

Al-Hajj (pilgrimage): visiting the House of God, the Exalted, to perform specific acts of worship called nusuk (sing. nusk).

Al-'Umrah (minor pilgrimage): visiting the House of God to circumambulate it, perform the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwa, and exit the state of ihram by shaving or shortening the hair of the head.

Al-junah (blame/sin): sin, and what follows from violating the command, either by abandoning an obligation or by doing what is forbidden.

Yattawwaf (yatawwaf): he runs (sa'a) between them, going and returning.

Khayran (goodness): Khayr is a name for everything that brings joy and repels harm, and what is meant here is righteous deeds.

The meaning of the noble verse:

He, the Exalted, informs us, affirming the obligation of the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwa, and removing what some believers imagined: that there is sin in performing the sa'y between them, given that in the Jahiliyyah there was an idol on al-Safa called Isaf, and another on al-Marwa called Na'ila, and those who performed the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwa would rub against them. So the Exalted said: "Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwa [i.e., the sa'y between them] are among the sha'a'ir of God," meaning one of His acts of worship, since His Prophet Ibrahim and his son Isma'il, and the Muslims from their progeny, were commanded to perform the sa'y between them. Therefore, whoever makes the pilgrimage to the House to perform the Hajj obligation, or performs the 'Umrah to fulfil its obligation, let him perform the sa'y between them as fulfilment of a pillar of Hajj and 'Umrah, and there is no sin upon him because the polytheists used to perform the sa'y between them for the sake of the two idols, Isaf and Na'ila.

Then the Exalted informed, promising His servant believers, that whoever among them voluntarily does any good deed, He will reward him for it and recompense him, because He, the Exalted, is Appreciative of His servants' righteous deeds and rewards them for them, knowing those deeds and the intentions of their doers. This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever volunteers good, then indeed Allah is Appreciative and Knowing﴾.

Guidance of the noble verse:

Among the guidance of this verse:

1- The obligation of the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwa for everyone who circumambulates the House, whether performing Hajj or 'Umrah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Perform sa'y, for Allah has prescribed for you the sa'y." (Narrated by al-Daraqutni, and it was not found to have a defect.) The Prophet (ﷺ) performed the sa'y in all of his 'Umrahs and likewise in his Hajj.

2- There is no harm in praying in a church that has been converted into a mosque, and it does not matter that it had previously been a place of worship for disbelievers.

3- Encouragement to perform good deeds beyond the obligatory acts, such as all voluntary acts of worship: circumambulation, prayer, fasting, charity, guarding the frontier (ribat), and jihad.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 159–162:

Explanation of the words:

Yaktumun (they conceal): they hide and cover up, so that the concealed matter does not appear or become known and thus is not acted upon.

Al-bayyinat (the clear proofs): plural of bayyinah, which is that by which a thing is established as proven. What is meant here is what establishes the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) through the descriptions and attributes that came in the books of the People of the Book.

Al-huda (the guidance): that which indicates the correct goal and helps one reach it. What is meant here is the sound religion brought by the Messenger of Allah, which leads whoever adheres to it to perfection and happiness in this world and the Hereafter.

Fi al-kitab (in the Book): the Torah and the Gospel.

Al-la'nah (the curse): expulsion and distance from every good and mercy.

Al-la'inun (those who curse): those from whom cursing proceeds, such as the angels and the believers.

Aslahu (they reform): correcting what they had corrupted of people's beliefs and matters of religion, by making manifest what they had concealed and by believing in what they had denied and rejected.

Wa la hum yunzarun (nor will they be reprieved): that is, that they be given respite to make excuses, as in His saying, Most High: ﴿And it will not be permitted for them, so they will not make excuse﴾ [Al-Mursalat: 36].

Meaning of the verses:

After answering the scruple of some Muslims about performing the sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwah, the context returns to denouncing the crimes of the scholars of the People of the Book and calling them to repentance by manifesting the truth and believing in it. So Allah, Most High, informs that those who conceal what He sent down of clear proofs and guidance in the Torah and the Gospel, concerning the attributes of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and the command to believe in him and in what he brought of religion, these distant ones are cursed by Allah, Most High, and cursed by the angels and the believers. This is what the first verse [159] contains. In the verse that follows [160], Allah, Most High, makes an exception from those distanced from His mercy: whoever of those concealers of the truth repents after having known it, then clarifies and reforms, these He accepts in forgiveness and shows mercy to them, for He is the Ever-Relenting, the Most Merciful.

In the third verse [161] and the fourth [162], Allah, Most High, informs that those who disbelieved, from the People of the Book and others, in His Messenger and his religion, and did not repent, dying in their disbelief, upon them is the curse of Allah, the angels and all people. Therefore they are expelled and distanced from the divine mercy, which is Paradise, and they abide forever in Hell, its punishment not being lightened for them, nor are they given respite to make excuses.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The prohibition of concealing knowledge. In the sound hadith: "Whoever conceals knowledge, Allah will bridle him with a bridle of fire." Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) said in certain circumstances: "Were it not for a verse in the Book of Allah, I would not have related a hadith to you," and he recited ﴿Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs...﴾ etc.

2- The condition for the repentance of one who has corrupted through his wrongdoing and ignorance is to reform what he corrupted by clarifying what he distorted, changed or altered, by manifesting what he concealed, and by returning what he took unjustly.

3- Whoever among mankind disbelieves and dies in his disbelief will, after his death, be cast into Hell, abiding forever in punishment, eternally, its punishment not lightened for him, nor is he given respite to make excuse, nor is the punishment relaxed for him so that he may rest.

4- The permissibility of cursing those who openly commit sins, such as drinkers of wine and usurers, and men who imitate women and women who imitate men.

So Allah, Most High, informs that those who conceal what He sent down of clear proofs and guidance in the Torah and the Gospel, concerning the attributes of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and the command to believe in him and in what he brought of religion, these distant ones are cursed by Allah, Most High, and cursed by the angels and the believers. This is what the first verse [159] contains. In the verse that follows [160], Allah, Most High, makes an exception from those distanced from His mercy: whoever of those concealers of the truth repents after having known it, then clarifies and reforms, these He accepts in forgiveness and shows mercy to them, for He is the Ever-Relenting, the Most Merciful.

In the third verse [161] and the fourth [162], Allah, Most High, informs that those who disbelieved, from the People of the Book and others, in His Messenger and his religion, and did not repent, dying in their disbelief, upon them is the curse of Allah, the angels and all people. Therefore they are expelled and distanced from the divine mercy, which is Paradise, and they abide forever in Hell, its punishment not being lightened for them, nor are they given respite to make excuses.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The prohibition of concealing knowledge. In the sound hadith: "Whoever conceals knowledge, Allah will bridle him with a bridle of fire." Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) said in certain circumstances: "Were it not for a verse in the Book of Allah, I would not have related a hadith to you," and he recited ﴿Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs...﴾ etc.

2- The condition for the repentance of one who has corrupted through his wrongdoing and ignorance is to reform what he corrupted by clarifying what he distorted, changed or altered, by manifesting what he concealed, and by returning what he took unjustly.

3- Whoever among mankind disbelieves and dies in his disbelief will, after his death, be cast into Hell, abiding forever in punishment, eternally, its punishment not lightened for him, nor is he given respite to make excuse, nor is the punishment relaxed for him so that he may rest.

4- The permissibility of cursing those who openly commit sins, such as drinkers of wine and usurers, and men who imitate women and women who imitate men.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 163–164:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Ilah (the one worshipped): the one who is worshipped, rightly or wrongly. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the true Ilah, the one worshipped in truth.

Wa-ilahukum ilahun wahid (And your God is One God): One in His essence and attributes; in His lordship (rububiyyah), so there is no creator, no provider, and no manager of the universe and of life except Him; and in His divinity (uluhiyyah), that is, in worship, so there is no one worthy of worship in truth besides Him.

Ikhtilaf al-layl wa-l-nahar (the alternation of night and day): by the presence of one of them and the absence of the other, for the benefit of the servants, such that the day is not perpetual nor the night perpetual.

Wa-batha fiha min kulli dabbah (and He scattered in it every kind of creature): He dispersed and spread throughout the earth all kinds of creeping creatures.

Tasrif al-riyah (the turning of the winds): by their varying directions, sometimes a breeze (saba), sometimes a western wind (dabur), sometimes a northern wind, sometimes a western wind; or sometimes fertilizing and sometimes barren.

Meaning of the two verses:

When Allah made it obligatory upon the scholars to clarify knowledge and guidance and forbade them to conceal them, He informed that He is the One God, the Merciful, the Compassionate, and that this is the first thing the scholars must make clear to the people: His oneness in His lordship, His worship, and His names and attributes. When some of the polytheists heard the affirmation of this truth, "And your God is One God," they said: "What is the proof?" meaning proof that there is no god but Allah. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ up to His saying ﴿who reason﴾, comprising six cosmic signs, each one a clear proof and decisive evidence of the existence of Allah, His power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy, all of which necessitate worshipping Him alone, to the exclusion of anyone else.

The first: the creation of the heavens and the earth, a great creation that can only be accomplished by the Capable, whom nothing can overpower.

The second: the alternation of night and day through their succession and the lengthening of this and the shortening of that.

The third: the sailing of the ship (al-fulk), the ships, upon the sea despite their massiveness and size, carrying hundreds of tons of provisions and what people benefit from in their lives.

The fourth: His sending down rain from the sky for the life of the earth through plants and crops after its barrenness and death.

The fifth: the turning of the winds, hot and cold, fertilizing and non-fertilizing, eastern, western, northern and southern, according to the needs of people and what their lives require.

The sixth: the clouds subjected between heaven and earth, their formation and their driving from one land to another, so that it rains here and does not rain there, according to the will of the Mighty, the Wise.

In these six signs there is the greatest proof and the strongest evidence of the existence of Allah, exalted is He, His knowledge, power, wisdom and mercy; and for this reason He is the Lord of the worlds and the God of the first and the last, and there is no lord other than Him and no god besides Him. However, the one who perceives these proofs and sees them manifest in the mentioned signs is the one who has reason; as for the one who has no reason, because he has disabled his intellect, not using it for reflection, understanding and comprehension, and has used desire instead of intellect, then he is blind who sees nothing, deaf who hears nothing, and foolish who understands nothing, and we seek refuge with Allah, exalted is He.

Guidance from the two verses:

Among the guidance of the two verses:

1- There is no god but Allah, so worship is not valid for anyone other than Allah, exalted is He, for there is no true god except Him.

2- The cosmic signs in the heavens and the earth establish the existence of Allah, exalted is He, as Lord and God, described with every perfection and free from every deficiency.

3- The revealed Qur'anic verses establish the existence of Allah as Lord and God, establish Muhammadan prophethood, and affirm his mission (ﷺ).

4- Benefiting from the signs in general, whether the verses of the Book or the signs of the cosmos, is restricted to those who use their intellects rather than their desires.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 165–167:

Explanation of the words:

Andadan (ﺃَﻧْﺪَﺍﺩًﺍ): plural of nidd, meaning a equal, a peer, or a likeness. Here "andad" refers to partners whom they worship by loving them, drawing near to them through various acts of worship such as supplication, vowing to them, and swearing by them.

Tabarri' (التبرؤ): disowning a thing and distancing oneself from it out of aversion.

Alladhina ittubi'u (الذين اتُّبعوا): the worshipped ones and the misleading leaders.

Alladhina ittaba'u (الذين اتَّبعوا): the polytheists and those who follow their leaders in error by imitation.

Al-asbab (الأسباب): plural of sabab, which linguistically means a rope, then came to be used for everything that connects two things and for everything by which one reaches a particular aim or purpose.

Karrah (كرَّة): a return and a coming back to the worldly life.

Al-hasarat (الحسرات): plural of hasrah, meaning intense remorse that nearly wears out its bearer, so that it keeps him from movement and action.

Meaning of the verses:

Since it was established in the two preceding verses, by decisive proofs and clear evidence, that the God of mankind, that is their Lord and their object of worship, is one, namely Allah, may His majesty be exalted and His authority be great, He informed that, despite this clear explanation, there are people who take, besides Allah, gods, idols and leaders, whom they love as they love Allah, that is, they equate their love for them with the love of Allah. The believers, however, love Allah more intensely than they do. He also informed that if the polytheists could see, at the moment of facing the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, they would see a dreadful matter that words cannot describe, and they would know that power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment. When the followed ones, namely the oppressive leaders and callers to polytheism and misguidance, disown their followers, the ignorant imitators, and they witness the punishment before them, and those bonds that once connected them are cut off. The followers wish to return to the worldly life so that they may take revenge on their leaders in misguidance, disowning them in the world just as they disowned them in the Hereafter. Just as Allah showed them the punishment and they witnessed it, He will show them their ugly deeds of polytheism and sins, so their regret will intensify, their distress will grow severe, and they will enter the Fire with them and never come out of it.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation to love Allah, and to love everything that is loved for the sake of His love, may He be glorified.

2- Loving something alongside Allah is part of polytheism, while loving for the sake of Allah's love is part of monotheism.

3- On the Day of Resurrection all ties of friendship and kinship will be dissolved, and only the bond of faith and brotherhood in it will remain.

4- The disowning by the leaders of polytheism and misguidance, and the callers to evil and corruption, of those who obeyed them in the world and followed them in injustice, evil and corruption, and that this will not benefit them at all.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 168–170:

Explanation of the words:

Al-halal (the lawful): that from which the knot of prohibition has been loosed, i.e. what Allah the Exalted has permitted.

Al-tayyib (the good, the wholesome): that which is pure and not impure, and not repugnant that souls shrink from it.

Khutuwat al-shaytan (the steps of Satan): khutuwat is the plural of khutwa, the distance between the feet of a walker. What is meant here is the paths and ways of Satan that lead the servant to forbid what Allah has made lawful and to make lawful what He has forbidden.

Aduwwun mubin (a clear enemy): his enmity is manifest, and how could it not be, for he is the one who expelled our parents Adam and Eve from the Garden, and most of the evils and corruptions in the world are only through his whisperings and seduction.

Al-su' (evil): everything that distresses the soul and afflicts it with sorrow and grief, and it includes all sins.

Al-fahsha' (abomination): every ugly trait, such as fornication, sodomy, stinginess, and all sins of extreme ugliness.

Alfayna (we found): we found.

Meaning of the verses:

After the presentation of the states of the people of polytheism and sin and the bitter end they came to, which is abiding forever in the punishment of the Fire, the Lord of vast mercy calls out to all of mankind: ﴿O mankind, eat of what is on the earth, lawful and good﴾, which is His bounty and grace, lawful and good, since He has permitted it for them. As for what He has not permitted for them, there is no good for them in eating it, because of the harm it brings to their bodies and souls together. Then He forbade them to follow the traces of His enemy and theirs, for if they follow his steps he will lead them to where their misery and destruction lie. Their Lord informed them that Satan does not command them except with what harms their bodies and souls, and the evil (al-su'), which is everything that distresses the soul, and the abomination (al-fahsha'), which is the most ugly of deeds and the most corrupt of morals. Even more grievous than that, he commands them to lie against Allah, to say about Him what they do not know, so that they forbid and permit and legislate in the name of Allah, while Allah is free of that. This is a back-breaking matter, and we seek refuge in Allah the Exalted. Thus, when they turn away from the guidance of their Lord and follow the steps of Satan, their enemy, they commit evil, perpetrate abominations, make lawful and forbid, and legislate what Allah their Lord has not permitted. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them, "Follow what Allah has sent down," they said, "No, rather we follow what we found our fathers upon." Glory be to Allah! They follow what they found their fathers upon even if it was falsehood and misguidance. Do they imitate their fathers even though their fathers did not understand anything of the matters of the Law and religion, and were not guided to what contains righteousness and good?

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation to seek what is lawful and to be content with a livelihood from it, even if it is meager and scant.

2- The lawful is what Allah has permitted, and the unlawful is what Allah the Exalted has forbidden, so reason alone does not independently determine anything of this.

3- The prohibition of following the paths of Satan, which are every belief, statement, or action that Allah the Exalted has forbidden.

4- The obligation to keep far from every evil and abomination, for these are what Satan commands.

5- The prohibition of imitating one who has no knowledge or insight in religion.

6- The permissibility of following people of knowledge and adopting their statements and opinions derived from divine revelation, the Book and the Sunnah.

6- The permissibility of following people of knowledge and adopting their statements and opinions derived from divine revelation, the Book and the Sunnah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 171:

Explanation of the words:

Mathal (مثل): the description and the state (al-sifah wa'l-hal).

Yan'iq (ينعق): he shouts, and the noun is al-nai'q, which is shouting and raising the voice.

Al-du'a' (الدعاء): calling someone near, such as a believer calling on his Lord, "O Lord, O Lord."

Al-nida' (النداء): calling someone far away, such as the call to prayer (adhan al-salah).

Al-summ (الصم): plural of asamm, one who lacks the faculty of hearing, so he does not hear.

Al-bukm (البكم): plural of abkam, one who lacks the faculty of speech, so he does not speak.

La ya'qilun (لا يعقلون): they do not grasp the meaning of speech and do not distinguish between things, because the instrument of perception in them, which is reason (al-'aql), is disabled.

The meaning of the noble verse:

When the previous verse [170] censured imitation (taqlid) and those who imitate, who disable their senses and faculties, do what their leaders tell them, and carry out what they are commanded, accepting it without knowing why they did or why they abstained, this verse came with a wondrous image and a strange parable for those who disable their rational faculties and are content with following others in everything, until they have become like sheep, which their shepherd drives wherever he wishes. When he shouts to them calling them, they answer him, even if his call is to slaughter them. Likewise, when he calls to them from afar, they answer, while not knowing why they were called, for they do not hear or understand anything except the mere voice they have become accustomed to through long imitation and following without proof.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the example of those who disbelieve﴾ in their rigidity and in imitating their forefathers in shirk and error is like a flock which its shepherd, who is trusted over them, shouts at; when he cries out to them calling them or summoning them, they hear the voice and respond, but they do not know why they were called or why they were summoned, due to the lack of reason in them. This parable applies to everyone who calls the people of disbelief and error to faith and guidance: he, with those he calls, the disbelievers, the imitators, and the rigid people of error, is like the one who shouts, etc......

Guidance of the verse:

Among the guidance of this noble verse:

1- Consolation for those who call to God, the Exalted, when they face imitators among the people of shirk and error.

2- The prohibition of imitating the people of whims and innovations.

3- The obligation of seeking knowledge and understanding, so that a believer does not act or abstain except with knowledge of what he does and what he leaves.

4- One should only follow the people of knowledge and insight in religion, because following the ignorant amounts to imitation.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 172–173:

Explanation of the words:

Al-tayyibat (the good things): plural of tayyib, meaning the lawful (halal).

Wa-shkurū lillah (and be grateful to Allah): acknowledge the blessings of Allah upon you, praise Him for them, and spend them in what pleases Him.

In kuntum iyyahu ta'buduna (if it is Him that you worship): if you are obedient to Allah, submitting to His command and prohibition.

Harrama (He has forbidden): prohibited and barred.

Al-maytah (carrion): an animal that has died of its own accord without being slaughtered according to the proper rite (tadhkiyah).

Al-dam (blood): flowing blood that is poured out, not blood mixed into the flesh.

Al-khinzir (the swine): a foul animal known for eating filth and for lacking jealousy over its females.

Wa-ma uhilla bihi li-ghayri Allah (and that over which a name other than Allah has been invoked): al-ihlal means raising the voice with the name of the idol to whom the animal is slaughtered.

Udturra (compelled): forced and driven by necessity, because of the harm that has befallen him, whether from hunger or beating.

Ghayra baghin wa-la 'adin (neither desiring nor transgressing): the baghi is the wrongdoer who seeks what is not lawful for him, and the 'adi (transgressor) is one who exceeds what is his right to what is not his.

Al-ithm (sin): the effect of disobedience upon the soul, through darkening and corruption.

The meaning of the two noble verses:

After the previous verse [171] showed the state of the disbelievers who blindly follow their forefathers in polytheism and in forbidding what Allah has made lawful of livestock, when they dedicated to the idols the sawaib, the wasila, the ha'm and the bahira, the Almighty, Majestic, called out to His believing servants: O you who believe in Allah as Lord and God, in Islam as religion, and in Muhammad as Messenger, eat of the good things We have provided you and be grateful to Allah your Lord for the blessings He has bestowed upon you, of lawful meats, and do not forbid them as the imitators of the polytheists forbade them. He, exalted is He, has forbidden you only the eating of carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that over which other than Allah has been invoked. Yet whoever is driven by necessity, fearing for his own life, and eats, there is no sin upon him, on condition that he is not, during his journey, rebelling against the Muslims nor transgressing by cutting off the road upon them. This is because Allah is Forgiving toward His allies who turn repentant to Him, and Merciful to them; He does not leave them in constriction or hardship.

Guidance of the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The recommendation to eat of the good things of Allah's provision without extravagance.

2- The obligation to thank Allah by acknowledging the blessing to Him, praising Him for it, and not spending it on His disobedience.

3- The prohibition of eating carrion, flowing blood, the flesh of swine, and that over which other than Allah has been invoked.

4- The permissibility of eating from the aforementioned prohibited things in cases of necessity, which is fear of death, while observing the exception stated in the verse: ﴿neither desiring nor transgressing﴾.

5- The Prophet (ﷺ) permitted the eating of fish and locusts, which are from the category of carrion, and prohibited the eating of every animal with fangs among the predators and every bird with talons.
