Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 204–207:

Explanation of the words:

Yu'jibuka (يعجبك): it pleases you and you find it fine.

Fi al-dunya (في الدنيا): when he speaks about the affairs of this worldly life.

Alad al-khisam (ألد الخصام): fierce in contention, strong in dispute, owing to the glibness of his tongue.

Tawalla (تولى): he turned back and departed, or he held authority.

Al-harth wa al-nasl (الحرث والنسل): al-harth means crops, and al-nasl means animals.

Akhathat-hu al-'izzah bi al-ithm (أخذته العزة بالإثم): zeal and arrogance seized him on account of his sins, so he does not fear Allah.

Yashri nafsahu (يشري نفسه): he sells his self to Allah, the Exalted, by striving in His cause with his self and his wealth.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah, the Exalted, informs His Messenger and the believers about the condition of the hypocrites and of the sincere believers. He says, addressing the Messenger ﷺ: "And among the people is a man, a hypocrite, who makes his speech pleasing, and when he speaks, you are pleased with his words, because of the polish and splendour that they have. This is when he speaks about the affairs of the life of this world, unlike the affairs of the Hereafter, for he is ignorant of them and has no impetus to speak about them, since he is a disbeliever. And when he speaks, he calls Allah to witness that he believes what he says, and says to the Messenger ﷺ, 'Allah knows that I am a believer and that I love you,' and calls Allah to witness, 'that I am such-and-such...' And when he leaves your gathering and departs from you, ﴿he strives in the land﴾, that is, he walks in it with corruption, to destroy the crops and the animals by committing grave crimes, so that rain is withheld, the harvests wither, the land becomes barren, the beasts die, and offspring are cut off. And this deed of his is hated by Allah, the Exalted, so He does not love it nor the one who does it." Allah, the Exalted, also informs that when this hypocrite is commanded to do good or forbidden from evil, and it is said to him, "Fear Allah, do not do such-and-such, or leave such-and-such," he is seized by arrogance and zeal on account of the sins with which he is afflicted, so he does not fear Allah and does not turn to Him in repentance. Hell is sufficient recompense for his hypocrisy, his evil and his corruption; he spreads it as a bed from which he never departs, forever. ﴿And how wretched is the resting-place, Hell.﴾

Allah, the Exalted, also informs about the sincere believer, saying: "And among the people is a man, a believer of true faith, who sold his self and his wealth to Allah, seeking His pleasure and life in His neighbourhood in the Garden, the Abode of Peace." So Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And among the people is he who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah; and Allah is Kind to His servants.﴾ That is, Merciful to them.

It is said that the hypocrite man whose description is contained in the first three verses is al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, and that the believing man whose description is contained in the fourth verse [207] is Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Rumi, Abu Yahya. When the polytheists learned that he intended to emigrate to Madinah to join the Messenger ﷺ and his Companions, they said, "You will not go off with your self and your wealth to Muhammad. We will not allow you to emigrate unless you give us all your wealth." So he gave them all that he possessed and emigrated. When he reached Madinah and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him, he said to him: "The sale has profited, Abu Yahya; the sale has profited." Although the verses were revealed concerning al-Akhnas and Suhayb, the lesson lies in the generality of the wording and not in the specificity of the occasion. Al-Akhnas is an example of evil for everyone who has his characteristics, and Suhayb is an example of goodness and perfection for everyone who has his characteristics.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- A warning against being deceived by the eloquence and articulateness of a man who is not among the people of faith and sincerity.

2- The worst of people is he who corrupts the land by committing crimes, which causes corruption and destruction to people and livestock.

3- A man's saying "Allah knows" or "Allah bears witness" counts as an oath, so the believer should beware of saying it while knowing himself to be lying.

4- When a believer is told "Fear Allah," it is obligatory for him not to be angry or to resent the one who commands him to piety; rather he must acknowledge his sin, seek Allah's forgiveness, and immediately give up the disobedience.

5- Encouragement to strive in the cause of Allah with one's self and wealth, and the permissibility for a Muslim to give up all his wealth in the cause of Allah, without this being considered extravagance or wastefulness, since extravagance and wastefulness are in spending on sins and wrongdoing.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 208–210:

Explanation of the words:

As-silm (السلم): Islam.

Kaffah (كافة): all together; no one fails to enter Islam, and nothing of its laws or its rulings is left out.

Khutuwat ash-shaytan (خطوات الشيطان): his paths in calling to falsehood and adorning evil and ugliness.

Fa-in zalaltum (فإن زللتم): if you slip into error, that is, fall into transgression and sins.

Al-bayyinat (البينات): the proofs and evidences.

Hal yanzurun (هل ينظرون): ma yanzurun (what are they waiting for?); the interrogative here is used for negation.

Ad-zulal (الظلل): plural of zullah, that which shades, such as clouds, trees, or the like.

Al-ghamam (الغمام): thin white clouds.

Meaning of the two verses:

The Truthful and Exalted God calls His believing servants, commanding them to enter Islam wholly, such that they do not choose among its laws and rulings only what agrees with their interests and desires, accepting and acting upon it, and rejecting or neglecting what does not agree. Rather, they must accept the laws and rulings of Islam in their entirety. He forbade them to follow the steps of Satan in beautifying the ugly and adorning the reprehensible, for it is he who made some of the believers among the People of the Book see the glorification of Saturday and the prohibition of eating camel meat as beautiful, on the pretext that this is from the religion of God which the righteous of the Children of Israel followed. So this verse was revealed concerning them, commanding them and all the other believers to accept all the laws and rulings of Islam, and warning them of the consequence of following Satan, which is complete ruin, and this is what Satan desires, by reason of his enmity toward man. This is what the verse [208] contains.

As for the second verse [209], it contains the greatest threat and the severest warning for one whom Satan has caused to slip, so that he accepts some laws of Islam and rejects others, although he knows that Islam is true and its laws are more worthy of acceptance. God says: ﴿And if you slip after the clear proofs have come to you﴾, which are contained in the Book of God, the Qur'an, and clarified by the Messenger of God Muhammad (ﷺ). Then God will surely take vengeance upon you, for He is Almighty over His command, Wise in His management, and in fulfilling His promise and His threat.

As for the third verse [210], it contains an urging of those who delay in entering Islam, for they have no excuse in that, since the proof has been established and the clear path has become manifest. God says: ﴿Do they await only that God should come to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels?﴾ That is, what do they await? ﴿...except that there should come to them God in canopies of clouds, and the angels﴾. At that time they will believe, but such compelled faith does not benefit, since the punishment will then be inevitable by the just decree of God. God says: ﴿And the matter is decided﴾, meaning: when God comes to render the final judgment, and the affair returns to Him, He decides, and everything is concluded. So upon those hesitant and wavering ones who delay entering Islam, which is expressed as as-silm, because entering it in truth is peace, and leaving it or not entering it in truth is war, it is incumbent upon them to enter Islam. Truly, to Islam, O servants of God! For peace is better than war!

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation to accept all the laws of Islam, and the prohibition of choosing among them.

2- Whoever makes lawful what is forbidden, or abandons an obligation, is in that a follower of Satan.

3- The necessity of expecting punishment when major sins appear, lest one feel secure from the plotting of God.

4- Affirmation of the attribute of coming for the Lord, the Exalted: to render the final judgment on the Day of Resurrection.

5- The prohibition of procrastination and delay in repentance.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 211–212:

Explanation of the words:

Sal (اسأل): the two hamzas were dropped for ease of pronunciation (the original form being is'al, "ask").

Banu Isra'il (بني إسرائيل): the descendants of Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim; Isra'il is the epithet (laqab) of Ya'qub.

Ayah (آية): a sign that breaks the normal course of things, like the staff of Musa, which indicates that the one to whom Allah gives such signs is truly a messenger of Allah. Among the signs Allah gave the Children of Israel were the splitting of the sea for them, and the sending down of manna and quail upon them in the wilderness (al-tih).

Ni'mat Allah (نعمة الله): whatever good Allah bestows upon His servant that brings him joy and repels harm from him. The blessings of Allah are many.

Yaskharun (يسخرون): they belittle and mock.

Meaning of the two verses:

Allah the Exalted commands His Messenger to ask the Children of Israel about the many signs that Allah gave them, and how they disbelieved in them so that they did not benefit them at all. The purpose is to console him ﷺ for the grief he suffers from the failure of the People of the Book and the polytheists to believe in him and in the guidance he brought. Within this is a rebuke and reproof of the Jews for their disbelief in the signs of Allah and their insistence on not entering Islam. Then Allah the Exalted informed that whoever exchanges the blessing of Allah, which is Islam, for disbelief in Him and in His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the punishment of Allah will surely befall him, either in this world or in the Hereafter, because Allah is severe in punishment.

This is what the first verse [211] contains. As for the second verse [212], Allah the Exalted informed that Satan adorned for those who disbelieve in Allah and His laws the life of this world, so they desired it, worked for it, and came to see nothing other than it. Therefore they mocked the believers who renounce it, because of their knowledge of its passing away and its little benefit. They did not devote all their effort to gathering it and obtaining it, but turned to obeying their Lord and spent what was in their hands in the way of Allah, seeking His pleasure. He also informed that the believing, God-fearing people, on the Day of Resurrection, will be recompensed with the best and most complete reward: He will settle them in the Abode of Peace in 'Illiyyun, and He will humiliate their enemies who mocked them and disgrace them, settling them in the lowest level of the Fire.

He, the Exalted, is the Bountiful, the possessor of benevolence: when He provides for whomever He wills, He gives without reckoning, and that is due to the vastness of His grace and the greatness of what He has.

Lessons from the two verses:

Among the lessons of the two verses:

1. A warning against ingratitude for blessings, because of what results from it of painful punishment and severe retribution. Among the greatest blessings is the blessing of Islam; whoever disbelieves in it and turns away from it has exposed himself to the most severe and harshest punishments. What befell the Children of Israel of various kinds of humiliation and degradation for a long period is strong evidence, and what has befallen the Muslims on the day they turned away from Islam and substituted for it superstitions and then man-made laws is an even greater proof.

2. A warning against the adornment of the life of this world, desiring it, amassing it, forgetting the Hereafter and neglecting work for it. The people of this world today mock the people of the Hereafter; but the people of the Hereafter, the people of faith and piety, will be above them on the Day of Resurrection, for they will be in the high gardens while the others are in the lowest depths of the Fire.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 213:

Explanation of the words:

"Mankind was one community": before shirk appeared among them, they were one community upon Islam and tawhid, and this was before the people of Nuh.

"The prophets" (al-nabiyyun): the plural of nabi (prophet). What is meant by them is the messengers, since every nabi is a rasul (messenger), as evidenced by their mission, which rests on giving glad tidings and warning, and which is drawn from the Books of Allah the Exalted revealed to them.

"The Book" (al-kitab): a generic noun that includes all divine Books.

"Were given it" (utu-hu): were given it.

"The clear proofs" (al-bayyinat): the proofs and demonstrations that the messengers brought to them, which establish among them laws, rulings, and general guidance.

"Out of rivalry" (baghyan): al-baghy (rebellious transgression) is injustice and envy.

"The straight path" (al-sirat al-mustaqim): Islam, which leads its follower to happiness and perfection in both lives.

Meaning of the noble verse:

He, the Exalted, informs that the people, between Adam and Nuh, peace be upon them both, were for a long period one community upon the religion of Islam; none was worshipped among them except Allah the Exalted, until Shaytan adorned for some of them the worship of other than Allah the Exalted, so shirk and misguidance arose. Allah the Exalted then sent Nuh, peace be upon him, to guide them, and they divided into believer and disbeliever, monotheist and polytheist. The messengers followed one another, bearing the Books of Allah the Exalted, which contain the decisive judgment regarding everything they differ about. Then He, the Exalted, informed of His way with people, which is that those who differ concerning the Book, i.e., concerning the laws and rulings it contains, are those who were previously given it and whose clear proofs came to them. Envy and love of leadership, and preserving their interests, drive them to refuse what the Book brought. The Jews are the example of this way, for they were given the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah the Exalted, and clear proofs came to them through the hands of their prophets and messengers who worshipped Allah, yet they differed over many laws and rulings. What drove them to this was rebellious transgression and envy, and we seek refuge in Allah.

Allah the Exalted guided the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) concerning what the two groups of the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, differed about. Thus the Exalted said: ﴿So Allah guided those who believed﴾ to the truth concerning which those differing had disagreed. He guided them by His permission, His kindness, and His success, so to Him belongs praise and bounty. Among that truth which the People of the Book before us differed about and which Allah the Exalted guided us to:

1- Belief in Jesus as the servant and messenger of Allah. The Jews disbelieved in him, denied him, accused him of sorcery, and tried to kill him; the Christians deified him, made him a god alongside Allah, and said of him that he is the son of Allah. Exalted is Allah above having a consort or a son.

2- Friday, which is the best of days. The Jews took Saturday and the Christians took Sunday, and Allah the Exalted guided the community of Islam to it.

3- The qibla: the qibla of the father of the prophets, Ibrahim. The Jews faced Bayt al-Maqdis and the Christians faced the rising of the sun, and Allah guided the community of Islam to face the Ancient House, the qibla of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.

Guidance from the verse:

1- The origin is tawhid, and shirk is an accident that befell humanity.

2- The essential task of the messengers is giving glad tidings to those who believe and fear Allah, and warning those who disbelieve and transgress. They may be legislated to fight those who fight them, as this was legislated for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

3- Among the signs of a community's abandonment and its exposure to loss and destruction is that it differs over its Book and its religion, so they distort the words of Allah and alter His laws, seeking leadership and pursuing desires and partisan zeal. This is what the community of Islam suffers from today and before today, and it was the cause of the destruction of the Children of Israel.

4- The community of Islam that lives by the Book and the Sunnah in creed, worship, and judgment is the one intended by His words: ﴿So Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning which they differed, by His permission﴾.

5- Guidance is in the hand of Allah, so the servant should always seek guidance from Allah the Exalted, by repeatedly asking Him to guide him always to the truth.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 214:

Explanation of the words:

Am hasibtum (أم حسبتم): Did you think? (aẓanantum). Here "am" is the disjunctive (munqaṭi'ah) particle, which is interpreted as "bal" (rather) together with the hamza, and the interrogation is one of denial, rejecting their assumption, because it does not fit its proper place.

Lamma (لما): in the sense of the negative particle lam (not).

Mathal (مثل): a description and state of those who came before you.

Al-ba'sa' wa'l-darra' (البأساء والضراء): al-ba'sa' is hardship, from need and other things; al-darra' is sickness, wounds and killing.

Mata nasr Allah (متى نصر الله): the interrogation expresses impatience (istib'ad) for the help.

Meaning of the noble verse:

Allah the Exalted denounces the believers, who were in days of hardship and distress, for their assumption that they would enter Paradise without being tested and tried in their selves and their wealth, and that there would not befall them what befell others of hardship, adversity and convulsion (zilzal), which is agitation and anxiety from terrors, until the Messenger and the believers with him say, impatient for the victory they had been promised: "When will the help of Allah come?" Their Lord, the Exalted, answers them with His saying: ﴿Surely the help of Allah is near﴾.

Guidance of the noble verse

From the guidance of the verse:

1- Being tested by the legal obligations, among them striving (jihad) with one's self and wealth, is necessary for entering Paradise.

2- Encouragement to take the righteous as models and to follow them in action and patience.

3- The permissibility of human states in the messengers, such as anxiety and impatience for the divine promise while awaiting it.

4- An explanation of what befell the Messenger (ﷺ) and his Companions of hardship and trial during the days of jihad and the siege of the polytheists against them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 215:

Explanation of the words:

"min khayr" (of good): from wealth, since wealth is called "khayr" (good) by the term.

"al-aqrabin" (the nearest relatives): such as brothers and sisters and their children, paternal uncles and aunts and their children, and maternal uncles and aunts and their children.

"wa ma taf'alu min khayr" (and whatever good you do): "ma" is conditional and "min" is explanatory, and "khayr" here refers to all kinds of righteousness and beneficence.

"fa-inna Allaha bihi 'alim" (then indeed Allah is Knowing of it): the clause is a reason for the omitted, presumed response of the condition, meaning: He will reward you for it.

The meaning of the noble verse:

ʿAmr ibn al-Jamuh, who was a man of wealth, asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) what he should spend and on whom he should spend. So the verse was revealed in answer to his question, explaining that what is spent is wealth and all kinds of good, and that those most deserving of being spent upon are parents and the nearest relatives, and the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer. Allah the Exalted informed them that whatever good a servant does, Allah knows it and will recompense him for it, thereby encouraging the doing of good in general.

Guidance of the noble verse:

From the guidance of the verse:

1- Asking one who does not know, in order to learn, is the way of knowledge; hence they said: "Asking is half of knowledge."

2- The preferability of spending on those mentioned in the verse if the one spending is wealthy and they are poor and needy.

3- The encouragement to do good and Allah's promise of the fullest reward for it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 216:

Explanation of the words:

"Kutiba" (it has been prescribed): He made it obligatory with emphasis, so much so that it is as if it were written down.

"Al-qital" (fighting): Fighting the disbelievers through striving (jihad) against them until they embrace Islam or give the jizya (the tax levied on non-Muslim subjects).

"Kurhun" (something disliked): Disliked by your souls by nature.

"ʿAsā" (perhaps): This verb signifies hope and expectation, meaning that what it governs is hoped for and expected, not with certainty. However, if it comes from Allah, the Exalted, it conveys certainty.

Meaning of the noble verse:

The Exalted informs His Messenger and the believing servants that He has made fighting the polytheists and disbelievers obligatory for them, while He knows that it is disliked by them by their nature, because of the pains, hardships, and the loss of wealth and life that it involves. He informed them that what they dislike may be good for them, and what they love may be evil for them. Among this is jihad: it is disliked by them, yet it is good for them, because in it lies their honor, their victory, and the victory of their religion, together with a good reward and great recompense in the Hereafter. Likewise, abandoning jihad is loved by them, yet it is evil for them, because it emboldens their enemy to fight them, to violate their sanctity, and to desecrate the sanctities of their religion, together with a bad recompense in the Hereafter. This which the Exalted has informed them of, namely their love of things that are evil for them and their dislike of things that are good for them, is as He has informed, since Allah knew it before He created them. Allah knows and you do not know, so it is obligatory to submit to Allah, the Exalted, in His command and His law, while loving what He has commanded and legislated, and believing that it is good with no evil in it.

Guidance from the noble verse:

Among the guidance of the verse:

1- The obligation of jihad upon the Muslim community as long as there is strife on earth and polytheism in it.

2- Human ignorance of consequences makes him love what is disliked and dislike what is loved.

3- All of Allah's commands are good, and all His prohibitions are evil. Therefore, it is obligatory to carry out His commands and avoid His prohibitions.

**Explanation of the words (Sharh al-Kalimat)**

*Al-haram qital fihi*: that is, the forbidden (sacred) one. *Qital* is a substitute (badal ishtimal) for *al-haram*, since the question concerns fighting in the sacred month (Rajab).

*Kabir*: that is, a great sin.

*Sadd 'an sabil Allah*: turning away from the religion of Allah.

*Wa kufr bihi*: disbelief in Allah, exalted is He.

*Al-Masjid al-Haram*: Makkah, and the Sacred Mosque within it.

*Ahluhu*: the Prophet (ﷺ) and the emigrants (al-muhajirun).

*Akbar*: greater in burden (of sin).

*Al-fitnah*: polytheism and the persecution of the believers so that they would disbelieve.

*Habitat a'maluhum*: their deeds became void; their reward is nullified, so they will not be rewarded for them because of their apostasy.

*Hajaru*: they left their homes, fearing trial and persecution for the sake of Allah.

**The meaning of the two verses**

When Allah, exalted is He, informed that He had prescribed fighting upon the believers, the Prophet (ﷺ) sent a detachment (sariyyah) under the command of 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh to Batn Nakhlah to gather information about the condition of the disbelievers. Allah willed that 'Abd Allah and his men would encounter a caravan (*'ir*) of the Quraysh; they fought them, killed a man called 'Amr ibn al-Hadrami, captured two others, seized the caravan, and returned. This happened on the last day of Jumada al-Akhirah, which was the first night of Rajab.

The Quraysh were enraged and said: "Muhammad has made the sacred month lawful by fighting in it." Their voices were echoed by the Jews and the hypocrites in Madinah, to the extent that the Messenger (ﷺ) held back the caravan and the two captives and did not decide anything concerning them. 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh and his companions were subjected to great blame and reproach from most people. The matter remained so until Allah, exalted is He, revealed these two verses: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it.﴾ That is, about fighting in it. Respond to them, O our Messenger, and say to them: fighting in it is a great sin, but turning away from the religion of Allah and disbelieving in Him, exalted is He, as well as barring from the Sacred Mosque, and expelling the Messenger and the believers from it, while they are its people and its rightful custodians, is greater in burden in the judgment of Allah, exalted is He. Likewise, the polytheism of the polytheists within the Sacred Precinct and the trial of the believers in it, to turn them back from their true religion to disbelief through various kinds of torture, is greater than killing in the sacred month. In addition to all this, they are determined to fight the believers until they turn them back from their religion, if they are able. Then Allah, exalted is He, informed the believers, warning them against apostasy whatever the punishment: whoever apostatizes from his religion and does not repent, dying in disbelief, all his good deeds will be voided, and he will become one of the people of the Fire, abiding therein forever. This is what the first verse contains.

As for the second verse [218]: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who emigrated and strove in the way of Allah — those hope for the mercy of Allah, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ It was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh and his companions. Allah, exalted is He, reassured them that they were not sinful for fighting in the sacred month, even though people censured them for it; that they hope for the mercy of Allah, that is, Paradise; and that He, exalted is He, is Forgiving of their sins and Merciful toward them, because of their faith, their emigration, and their striving in the way of Allah.

**Guidance from the two verses (Hidayah al-Ayatayn)**

1. The sanctity of the sacred month and the sacred land.

2. The abrogation (naskh) of fighting in the sacred month, based on the Prophet's (ﷺ) fighting against Hawazin and Thaqif in Shawwal and the beginning of Dhu al-Qa'dah, both of which are among the sacred months.

3. Exposing the disposition of the disbelievers, namely their constant determination to fight the Muslims until they turn them back from Islam and drive them out of it.

4. Apostasy voids deeds; if the apostate repents, he resumes his deeds anew, and if he dies before repenting, he is among the people of the Fire, abiding therein forever.

5. Clarifying the virtue of faith, emigration, and striving in the way of Allah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 219–220:

Explanation of the words:

Al-khamr (wine, intoxicant): Everything that veils the intellect and covers it, so that the one who drinks it cannot discern or reason. The term khamr is applied to the juice of grapes, dates, barley and other things.

Al-maysir (gambling): Gambling. It is called maysir because its practitioner gains wealth with ease and facility.

Al-ithm (sin, harm): Everything harmful and corrupt that damages the self, the intellect, the body, wealth or honour.

Al-manafi' (benefits): The plural of manfa'ah, which is that which gives pleasure and does not harm, from all sayings, actions and materials.

Al-'afw (surplus): Here, al-'afw means what exceeds and remains beyond a person's need of wealth.

Tatafakkarun (you reflect): So that you know what benefits in each of them, and so that you act for your worldly life in what sets it right, and act for your hereafter in what makes you happy there and saves you from its punishment.

Takhalitunahum (you mix with them): You mix their wealth with your wealth so that it becomes equal.

La-a'natakum (would have burdened you): Al-'anat is severe hardship; it is said a'nathu when one imposes severe hardship upon him.

Meaning of the two verses:

In the Jahiliyyah, the Arabs used to drink wine and gamble. Then Islam came and began calling them to monotheism and belief in the Last Resurrection, for these two are the strong impetus towards uprightness in life. When the Messenger ﷺ and many of his Companions emigrated, and Madinah became an Islamic society, the rulings began to descend gradually. It happened one day that one of the Companions led a congregation in prayer while intoxicated, and he confused the recitation. Then the verse of al-Nisa' was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ [4:43], so they would not drink it except at specific times. Here, questions about drinking wine increased, so this verse was revealed: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾. God answered them with His saying: ﴿Say: In them is great sin and benefits for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit﴾. Because of this verse, many abandoned both drinking wine and playing games of chance. Others remained, and ʿUmar was eager to prohibit them absolutely and would say: (O God, make clear to us a sufficient clarification regarding wine). God answered him, and the verse of al-Ma'idah was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, indeed wine and gambling...﴾ [5:90] up to His saying ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ [5:91]. ʿUmar said: (We have desisted, our Lord). Thereby wine was prohibited and gambling was prohibited with complete and definitive prohibition. The Messenger ﷺ set the legal penalty for wine, which is flogging, and warned against drinking it, and called it the mother of all evils, and said: «The habitual drinker of wine—Allah will not speak to him on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify him—among three persons: the one who disobeys his parents, the one who lets his lower garment trail, and the habitual drinker of wine.»

As for His saying, Exalted is He, ﹛In them is great sin and benefits for people﹜, it is as He said. He explained in Surah al-Ma'idah the source of the sin, which is that they cause enmity and hatred among the Muslims and bar from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer. What greater sin is there than sowing enmity and hatred among the individuals of the Muslims, and turning away from the remembrance of Allah and neglecting the prayer? Truly, in them is great sin. As for the benefits, they are, beside this sin, few: among them is profit in trading and manufacturing wine, and what the drinker gains of exhilaration, joy, generosity and courage. As for gambling, among its benefits is obtaining wealth without toil or effort, and the benefit to some of the poor from it, for they used to gamble over a she-camel, then it would be slaughtered and given to the poor and needy.

As for His saying in the verse ﴿They ask you what they should spend﴾, it is a question that arose from their response to the saying of God, Exalted is He: ﴿And spend in the way of Allah﴾ [2:195]. They wished to know the portion they should spend of their wealth in the way of Allah, so Allah, blessed and exalted, answered them with His saying: ﴿Say: the surplus﴾, i.e., what exceeds your need and remains beyond your expenditure on yourselves. From here the Messenger ﷺ said: «The best charity is that which is given out of surplus wealth» (narrated by al-Bukhari). And His saying ﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses, that you may reflect upon this world and the Hereafter﴾ means: like this clarification, Allah makes clear to you the laws, rulings, the lawful and the unlawful, so that He may direct you thereby to conscious and perceptive reflection on the matter of this world and the Hereafter, so that you act for your worldly life according to your need of it, and act for your Hereafter, to which you will return and in which you will remain, according to that.

This is what the first verse [219] contained. As for the second verse [220], ﴿They ask you about orphans﴾, the verse: when the saying of God, Exalted is He, in Surah al-Nisa' was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly only consume fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a Blaze﴾ [4:10], the believing men and women feared this severe warning. Whoever had an orphan in his household under his care separated the orphan's food from his own food and his drink from his own drink, and great hardship and difficulty resulted. They asked about the way out, so this verse was revealed and explained to them that the intent is to set right the orphans' property, and not to separate it or mix it. God said: ﴿Say: setting it right for them is good....﴾ Mixing with correction is better than separation without correction. And to remove hardship in mixing, He said: ﴿And if you mix with them, they are your brothers﴾, and a brother mixes with his brother in his property. He informed them that God knows the one who corrupts the orphan's property from the one who sets it right, so that they may always be cautious. All of this is a protection of the property of the orphan who has lost his father. Then God increased His favour upon them by lifting hardship in mixing, and said: ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have burdened you﴾, i.e., He would have kept you in the hardship resulting from separating your property from the property of your orphans. His saying "indeed Allah is Mighty" means He prevails over what He wills, "Wise" in what He does and decrees.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The prohibition of wine and gambling, as this verse was abrogated by the verse of al-Ma'idah, because of His saying in it: ﴿so avoid it﴾ and His saying ﴿So will you not desist?﴾.

2- Explanation of the best voluntary charity, which is that given out of surplus wealth, and this is the meaning of al-'afw in this verse.

3- The recommendation of reflecting on the matters of this world and the Hereafter, to give the first its due according to its passing, and the Hereafter according to its permanence.

4- The permissibility of mixing an orphan's property with that of his guardian when that is more profitable and more advantageous for him, and this is the meaning of correction in the verse.

5- The sanctity of an orphan's property, and warning against touching it or mixing it when that would cause loss or corruption in it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 221:

Explanation of the words:

وَلَا تَنكِحُوا (wa-la tankihu): do not marry.

الأمة (al-amah): a female slave, as opposed to a free woman (al-hurrah).

وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ (wa-law a'jabatkum): even if her beauty pleases you, i.e., her beauty and attractiveness appeal to you.

يَدْعُونَ إِلَى النَّارِ (yad'una ila al-nar): they call to the Fire by their state, their speech and their deeds.

آيَاته (ayatihi): the rulings of His religion and the matters of His law.

Meaning of the noble verse:

God Most High forbids the believers to marry idolatresses unless they believe in God and His Messenger; if they believe, it is permissible to marry them. He clarifies the matter, warning against marrying idolatresses and encouraging marriage to believing women, saying: ﴿a believing slave-girl is better than a free idolatress, even if she pleases you﴾. Just as He forbade, as a prohibition, that they give believing women in marriage to idolaters until they believe, and if they believe it is permissible for them to marry them their daughters and women. God Most High said: ﴿And do not marry idolaters until they believe﴾, and He said, warning and encouraging: a believing slave is better than a free idolater, even if the idolater pleases them for his nobility, wealth or power. He gave the reason for this by saying: "Those" (i.e., the idolatresses and idolaters) "call to the Fire," so mixing with them is harmful and corrupting, especially by marrying them. God, Mighty and Majestic, calls to Paradise through faith and righteous deeds, and to forgiveness through sincere repentance. So respond to Him and obey Him in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you. Likewise, He Most High makes His signs clear to people so that they may be prepared for reflection and admonition, and they will turn to His obedience, which leads to His pleasure and Paradise, and turn away from His disobedience, which leads to His wrath and the Fire.

Guidance from the noble verse:

Among the lessons of the verse:

1- The prohibition of marrying idolatresses. As for women of the People of the Book, God Most High has permitted them by the verses of al-Ma'idah, when He said: ﴿And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 5].

2- The prohibition of a believing woman marrying a disbeliever absolutely, whether he is an idolater or a People of the Book.

3- The condition of a guardian (wali) in a woman's marriage, since His words "and do not marry" address the guardians of believing women here; therefore a marriage is not valid without a guardian.

4- Warning against mixing with idolaters and encouraging distance from them, because they call to disbelief by their state, their speech and their deeds, and thereby they call to the Fire.

5- The obligation of loyalty to the people of faith and enmity toward the people of disbelief and misguidance, because the former call to Paradise and the latter call to the Fire.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 222–223:

Explanation of the words:

Al-mahid (al-maḥīḍ): the place of menstruation and its time. Menstruation (ḥayḍ) is blood that comes out of a woman's womb when it is free of a fetus.

Adha (adhan): harm that afflicts the one who has intercourse during its days.

Fa'tazilu al-nisa' fi al-mahid: leave off having intercourse with them during the days of menstruation.

Wa la taqrabuhunna hatta yatahharna: that is, do not have intercourse with them until the menstrual blood stops.

Fa-idha tatahharna: that is, when the blood of their menstruation has stopped and they have performed the ritual bath (ghusl) from it.

Fa'tuhunna min haythu amarakum Allah: that is, have intercourse with them in their front passage (qubul), when they are pure and have purified themselves.

Nisa'ukum harthun lakum: he means the place of childbearing. He likened women to a tilled field, because when the earth is tilled it brings forth crops, and when a woman is taken in intercourse she brings forth a child, by the permission of God, may He be exalted.

Fa'tu harthakum anna shi'tum: a permission for intercourse with a woman from the front or from behind, provided that it is in the front passage, which is the place where crops grow, and that she is pure from menstruation and postnatal bleeding.

Wa qaddimu li-anfusikum: he means righteous deeds, among them the intention to guard oneself and one's wife chaste through intercourse, and the intention to beget righteous children who affirm the oneness of God and pray for their parents all their lives.

The meaning of the two verses:

God, may He be exalted, informs His Messenger that some of the believers asked him about menstruation: whether a woman may live with a man, eat and drink with him, or be entirely shunned until she is purified, since this was a custom of the people of the Jahiliyyah. He commanded him to tell them: menstruation is a harm that afflicts the man who has intercourse during it. Accordingly, they should keep away from menstruating women only in intercourse, not in companionship, eating or drinking, and only during the days of the flow of blood. Indeed, there is no harm in touching a menstruating woman in other than the area between the navel and the knee, according to the authentic hadith on this. He emphasised this prohibition by saying: "and do not approach them," that is, do not have intercourse with them, until they become pure by the cessation of their bleeding and the ritual bath after it, as He says: "when they have purified themselves," that is, bathed. "Then come to them as God has commanded you," that is, the front passage and not the rear, for that is forbidden. God, may He be exalted, informed them that He loves those who repent of sins and who purify themselves from impurities and filth, so let them repent and purify themselves in order to gain the love of their Lord, mighty and majestic. This is the meaning of the first verse [222].

As for the second verse [223], His saying: "Your women are a tilth for you," it contains the answer to a question, namely whether it is permissible for a man to have intercourse with a woman from behind, since this question was actually asked by some of them. God, may He be exalted, informed them that there is no bar to this provided it is in the front passage and the woman is pure from the blood of menstruation and postnatal bleeding. He called the woman a tilth because her womb is where a child grows, as crops grow in good soil. Since this is so, let a man come to his wife as he wishes, facing or from behind, since the purpose, which is chastity and the seeking of offspring, is attained. Thus His saying "as you wish" means in whatever manner you wish, facing or from behind, on the condition that it be in the front passage and not the rear. Then God admonished His servants with His saying: "And send ahead for yourselves something good," that is, good deeds that will benefit you in your hereafter, and know that you will meet God, so do not neglect His remembrance and obedience, for this is the provision that will benefit you on the day you stand before your Lord.

Finally, He commanded His Messenger to give good tidings to the believers of the good of this world and the next, and of their happiness in both, to those whose faith is sound and bears fruit in piety and righteous action.

Guidance from the two verses:

1. The prohibition of intercourse during menstruation and postnatal bleeding because of the harm in it, and because of His saying: "So keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them until they are purified."

2. The prohibition of intercourse with a woman once her menstrual or postnatal bleeding has stopped, if she has not yet bathed, because of His saying: "When they have purified themselves, then come to them."

3. The prohibition of anal intercourse with a wife, because of His saying: "Then come to them as God has commanded you," which is the front passage.

4. The obligation of purifying oneself from sins through repentance, and purifying oneself from filth and impurities with water.

5. The obligation to send ahead as much righteous deed as possible, to be the provision of the Muslim for the abode of the hereafter, because of His saying: "And send ahead for yourselves."

6. The obligation of fearing God by doing what He has commanded and abstaining from what He has forbidden and warned against.

7. God's good tidings, through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ), to every believing man and woman.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 224–227:

Explanation of the words:

Al-'Ur-da (obstacle): that which is placed as a barrier against something; and the oath which a believer swears not to do good.

Al-Aymān (oaths): the plural of yamīn (oath), such as "By God, I will not do such-and-such," or "By God, I will certainly do such-and-such."

Al-Birr (righteousness): obedience and the doing of good.

Al-Laghw (idle talk): falsehood, and that which contains no good. The idle oath (laghw al-yamīn) is when a person swears about something he thinks is so, and it turns out to be otherwise; or it is what runs on the tongue of oaths without intending to swear.

Kasabat qulūbukum (what your hearts have earned): what the heart deliberately intends and purposes the oath for, such as to do something definitely or to prevent it.

Yu'lūn (those who swear off): al-Īlā' (swearing off) is swearing not to have intercourse with one's wife.

Al-Tarabbus (waiting): waiting and deliberation.

Fā'ū (they return): they returned to having intercourse with their wives after abstaining from it by oath.

Al-Ṭalāq (divorce): dissolving the bond of marriage and ending it by saying "you are divorced," "you are divorced," or "I divorce you."

Meaning of the verses:

God, blessed and exalted, forbids His believing servants to make swearing by Him an obstacle to doing good. This is like a person swearing that he will not give charity to so-and-so, or that he will not speak to so-and-so, or that he will not reconcile two people. So God said: ﴿And do not make Allah the target of your oaths as an obstacle to righteousness and piety and reconciliation between people﴾. He informed them that He is All-Hearing of their words and All-Knowing of their intentions and deeds, so let them fear Him, Mighty and Majestic.

Then He informed them that He does not hold them accountable for idle talk in their oaths, which is when a man swears about something he thinks is so, and it appears to be contrary to what he thought, or when what runs on his tongue of oaths is not intended, such as saying "No, by Allah," or "Yes, by Allah." This is among what God has pardoned for His servants, so there is no sin in it and no expiation that is required for it. But He holds them accountable for what their hearts have earned of sin, such as when a person swears falsely to take his Muslim brother's right by his false oath. This is the perjurious oath (al-yamīn al-ghamūs), which plunges its swearer into sin and then into the Fire. Expiation, which is prescribed for one who swears not to do something or to do it and then breaks the oath, does not benefit in this case. Rather, the perjurer's duty is repentance by denouncing himself, acknowledging his sin, and returning the right he took by his wicked oath to its owner. By this God forgives him and has mercy on him, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.

In connection with the mention of oaths, God mentioned the ruling on one who swears off from his wife, that is, swears not to have intercourse with her. God informed that the one who swears off must wait four months. If he returns to his wife, that is, returns to intercourse with her, then it is good and well; he must also expiate his oath. If he does not return to intercourse with her and persists in that, the judge must make him stand before him and demand that he return, and if he refuses, the judge divorces her on his behalf.

God said: ﴿For those who swear off from their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. Then if they return, indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. He forgives them the sin they committed against their wives and has mercy on them for their repentance.

And if they resolve on divorce, by refusing to return, then they have divorced, and God is All-Hearing of their words and All-Knowing of what is in their hearts.

So let them beware of Him by not doing what He dislikes and by abandoning what He loves.

Guidance of the verses:

1- Disapproval of preventing good because of an oath. Accordingly, whoever swears not to do good should expiate his oath and do the good, based on the authentic hadith: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, let him expiate his oath and do what is better."

2- The idle oath is pardoned, and it has two forms. The first is that the wording of an oath runs on the tongue while he does not intend to swear, such as "No, by Allah" and "Yes, by Allah." The second is that he swears about something he thinks is so and it turns out otherwise, such as saying, "By Allah, there is not a dirham or a dinar in my pocket," while he supposes or is certain there is nothing of that in his pocket, and then he finds it. This is the form of idle oath.

3- The oath for which the servant is held accountable is one in which he deliberately swears to a falsehood, intending it in order to obtain a worldly benefit. This is what is meant by God's words: ﴿But He holds you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾, and it is called the perjurious oath (al-yamīn al-ghamūs) and the wicked oath (al-yamīn al-fājira).

4- The oath in which expiation is required is one in which the servant swears to do something and then is unable and does not do it, or swears not to do something and then is compelled and does it, and he did not say "if God wills" while swearing. The expiation is specified in the verse of al-Mā'ida: feeding ten needy persons, or clothing them, or freeing a slave; and if one cannot find these, he fasts three days.

5- Explanation of the ruling on al-īlā': a man swears not to have intercourse with his wife for a period. If the period is less than four months, he may not break his oath and may continue abstaining from intercourse until the period of the oath ends; however, it is better that he have intercourse and expiate his oath. If the period is more than four months, he must return to his wife, or she is divorced against his will, even if he is angry and unwilling.
