This is like a person swearing that he will not give charity to so-and-so, or that he will not speak to so-and-so, or that he will not reconcile two people. So God said: ﴿And do not make Allah the target of your oaths as an obstacle to righteousness and piety and reconciliation between people﴾. He informed them that He is All-Hearing of their words and All-Knowing of their intentions and deeds, so let them fear Him, Mighty and Majestic.

Then He informed them that He does not hold them accountable for idle talk in their oaths, which is when a man swears about something he thinks is so, and it appears to be contrary to what he thought, or when what runs on his tongue of oaths is not intended, such as saying "No, by Allah," or "Yes, by Allah." This is among what God has pardoned for His servants, so there is no sin in it and no expiation that is required for it. But He holds them accountable for what their hearts have earned of sin, such as when a person swears falsely to take his Muslim brother's right by his false oath. This is the perjurious oath (al-yamīn al-ghamūs), which plunges its swearer into sin and then into the Fire. Expiation, which is prescribed for one who swears not to do something or to do it and then breaks the oath, does not benefit in this case. Rather, the perjurer's duty is repentance by denouncing himself, acknowledging his sin, and returning the right he took by his wicked oath to its owner. By this God forgives him and has mercy on him, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.

In connection with the mention of oaths, God mentioned the ruling on one who swears off from his wife, that is, swears not to have intercourse with her. God informed that the one who swears off must wait four months. If he returns to his wife, that is, returns to intercourse with her, then it is good and well; he must also expiate his oath. If he does not return to intercourse with her and persists in that, the judge must make him stand before him and demand that he return, and if he refuses, the judge divorces her on his behalf.

God said: ﴿For those who swear off from their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. Then if they return, indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. He forgives them the sin they committed against their wives and has mercy on them for their repentance.

And if they resolve on divorce, by refusing to return, then they have divorced, and God is All-Hearing of their words and All-Knowing of what is in their hearts.

So let them beware of Him by not doing what He dislikes and by abandoning what He loves.

Guidance of the verses:

1- Disapproval of preventing good because of an oath. Accordingly, whoever swears not to do good should expiate his oath and do the good, based on the authentic hadith: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, let him expiate his oath and do what is better."

2- The idle oath is pardoned, and it has two forms. The first is that the wording of an oath runs on the tongue while he does not intend to swear, such as "No, by Allah" and "Yes, by Allah." The second is that he swears about something he thinks is so and it turns out otherwise, such as saying, "By Allah, there is not a dirham or a dinar in my pocket," while he supposes or is certain there is nothing of that in his pocket, and then he finds it. This is the form of idle oath.

3- The oath for which the servant is held accountable is one in which he deliberately swears to a falsehood, intending it in order to obtain a worldly benefit. This is what is meant by God's words: ﴿But He holds you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾, and it is called the perjurious oath (al-yamīn al-ghamūs) and the wicked oath (al-yamīn al-fājira).

4- The oath in which expiation is required is one in which the servant swears to do something and then is unable and does not do it, or swears not to do something and then is compelled and does it, and he did not say "if God wills" while swearing. The expiation is specified in the verse of al-Mā'ida: feeding ten needy persons, or clothing them, or freeing a slave; and if one cannot find these, he fasts three days.

5- Explanation of the ruling on al-īlā': a man swears not to have intercourse with his wife for a period. If the period is less than four months, he may not break his oath and may continue abstaining from intercourse until the period of the oath ends; however, it is better that he have intercourse and expiate his oath. If the period is more than four months, he must return to his wife, or she is divorced against his will, even if he is angry and unwilling.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 228:

Explanation of the words:

Al-mutallaqat (the divorced women): the plural of mutallaqah, meaning a woman whose companionship has become bad, so that her husband or the judge divorces her.

Yatarabbasna (they shall wait): they shall await.

Quru' (menstrual cycles or periods of purity): al-qur' is either the period of purity (ṭuhr) or the period of menstruation (ḥayd).

Ma khalaqa Allah fi arhamihinna (what Allah has created in their wombs): this refers to the fetuses, so it is not lawful for the divorced woman to conceal it.

Ba'uluhunna (their husbands): their husbands. The singular of bu'ulah is ba'l, on the pattern of fahl and nakhl.

Bi-raddihinna fi dhalika (to take them back during that): that is, during the period of waiting and expectation.

Wa lahunna mithl alladhi 'alayhinna (and they have rights similar to those they owe): meaning that the wife has rights upon her husband, just as he has rights upon her.

Wa lil-rijali 'alayhinna darajah (but men have a degree over them): this is the degree of qawwamah, namely that the man, according to the Law, is the guardian (qayyim) over the woman.

The meaning of the noble verse:

On the occasion of the divorce of the one who takes an oath to abstain (mu'li) if he insists on not returning to his wife, the Exalted mentions in this verse, ﴿And the divorced women﴾, etc., that a woman who menstruates must wait and not expose herself to marriage for a period of three menstrual cycles. If the period ends and her husband has not taken her back, she may then marry. This waiting is called 'iddah, and it is obligatory and imposed upon her for the right of her husband, since he has the right to take her back during it. This is the meaning of His saying in the verse: ﴿And their husbands have the better right to take them back in that [period], if they desire reconciliation.﴾

Likewise, the divorced woman must not conceal menstruation, by saying, "I have menstruated only once or twice," while she has menstruated three times, wishing thereby to return to her husband; nor should she say, "I have menstruated three times," when she has not menstruated, in order that she not return to her husband. Nor should she conceal pregnancy, so that if she marries another man she attributes the child to him when it is not his child; this is one of the major sins. Therefore He, the Exalted, said: ﴿and it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, if they believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾, meaning menstruation and pregnancy. His saying: ﴿And their husbands have the better right to take them back in that﴾ means: the husband has the better right to his divorced wife as long as she is within her 'iddah, on condition that he does not intend by taking her back to harm her, but rather he must intend by her return reconciliation and good companionship between them. This is evident from His saying: ﴿if they desire reconciliation﴾. The divorced woman too must intend by her return to her husband reconciliation.

Then the Exalted informed that the wife has rights upon her husband similar to what the husband has upon her, so He said: ﴿And they have rights similar to those upon them, according to what is reasonable﴾. He also informed that men have a degree over women which women have not attained and did not possess, namely the qawwamah understood from His saying in Surat an-Nisa': ﴿Men are in charge of women by [right of] what Allah has given one over the other and what they spend from their wealth﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:34]. The verse concludes with the phrase ﴿And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise﴾, indicating the obligation to implement these teachings, because of the might and wisdom of Allah; for the mighty must be obeyed, and the wise must be submitted to in His legislation, since it is righteous, beneficial, and not harmful.

Guidance of the verse

From the guidance of the verse:

1- Explanation of the 'iddah of a divorced woman who menstruates, which is waiting for three menstrual cycles or three periods of purity.

2- The prohibition of a divorced woman concealing menstruation or a pregnancy that Allah has created in her womb, for whatever purpose.

3- The husband's right to take back his divorced wife if her 'iddah has not expired, to the extent that it has been said the one taken back is a wife, as evidenced by the fact that if she dies he inherits from her and if he dies she inherits from him. And it is not lawful for her to be proposed to or to marry while she is within her 'iddah.

4- Establishing the rights of each spouse over the other.

5- Affirming the authority of the man over the woman because of the qualities of manhood that Allah bestowed upon him, which are absent in the woman.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 229:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Talaq (divorce): the noun from "tallaqa," which is for a man to say to his wife, "You are divorced (anti talaq)," or "I have divorced you (tallaqtuki)."

Marratan (twice): he divorces her, then takes her back, then divorces her again, then takes her back. That is, the husband has the right of return after two divorces. But if he divorces her a third time, he has no right to that, and she does not return to him until she marries another husband.

Fa-in khiftum alla yuqima hudud Allah (and if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah): good companionship. If the wife or the husband fears that the marital rights will not be fulfilled, then ransom (fida') is permissible, which is the giving of property to the husband so that he releases the woman to go wherever she wishes. This is called khul' (khul').

Hudud Allah (the limits of Allah): what the servant must stop at in obedience to Allah and must not exceed.

Al-zalim (the wrongdoer): one who transgresses what Allah, exalted is He, has set as limits. Zulm (wrongdoing) is placing a thing in other than its proper place.

Meaning of the noble verse

The context still concerns the explanation of the rulings on divorce. In this verse, Allah, exalted is He, establishes that the divorce in which the husband has the right of return is two divorces only, the first and the second. Hence, whoever divorces for a second time is faced with two choices: either he keeps his wife with kindness, or he releases her with goodness. If he divorces her, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband. This is the meaning of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Divorce is twice; then either keep (them) in an acceptable manner or release (them) with good treatment﴾, i.e., with good companionship, which is fulfilling the husband's rights; or release (tasrih), i.e., divorce with goodness, by giving her the rest of her dowry if any, providing her with some property, and not mentioning her with evil.

And His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾: Allah, exalted is He, has forbidden the husband to take any of his wife's dowry without her consent, except in one case: when the woman dislikes the husband and cannot bear to remain with him, and he is not wronging her in this situation, it is permissible for her to give the husband property and he divorces her. This is called khul', and it is lawful for the husband who is not a wrongdoer. This is the meaning of ﴿But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾, and these here are good companionship. ﴿There is no blame upon them for what she ransoms herself with﴾, i.e., there is no sin upon them in what she ransoms herself with. So she may give the property to the husband, and he may take it from her in exchange for her release and the dissolution of the marital bond between them.

And His words, exalted is He: ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾, meaning the rulings of His law. So it is not lawful to go beyond the permissible to the forbidden, nor from kindness to harm, nor from what is right to what is wrong. ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah – it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾; he has wronged himself by exposing it to punishment, and it is not fitting for him to do so.

Lessons of the verse

From the lessons of the verse:

1- The prohibition of pronouncing three divorces with a single word, since Allah, exalted is He, said: "Divorce is twice."

2- A woman divorced three times is not lawful to her husband until she marries another husband who divorces her or dies leaving her.

3- The legitimacy of khul', which is when a woman dislikes remaining with her husband and releases herself from him with property she gives him in exchange for what he spent on her in marrying her.

4- The obligation to stop at the limits of Allah and the prohibition of transgressing them.

5- The prohibition of wrongdoing, which has three types: the wrongdoing of shirk, which is not forgiven for the servant except by repentance from it; the servant's wrongdoing against his fellow human, which must be settled by seeking his pardon; and the servant's wrongdoing against himself by transgressing one of the limits of Allah, whose matter is up to Allah: if He wills, He forgives it, and if He wills, He punishes for it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 230:

Explanation of the words:

*Fa-in tallaqahā fa-lā tahillu lahu* ("Then if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him"): the third divorce; she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband.

*Fa-lā junāḥa ʿalayhimā* ("Then there is no blame upon the two of them"): that is, there is no sin or fault upon them in marrying again.

*An yatarājaʿā* ("to return to one another"): that each of them returns to the other by a new contract, on condition that they think they will uphold the limits of Allah between them; otherwise, their marriage is not permissible.

The meaning of the noble verse:

Allah, exalted is He, says, explaining the ruling for one who divorces his wife a third time: *Then if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband* (ḥattā tankiḥa zawjan ghayrahu), and the marriage must be valid, and the second husband must consummate it (yabnī bihā), based on the hadith, "Until you have tasted his sweetness and he has tasted yours." If the second husband divorces her after consummation, seclusion and intercourse, or dies leaving her, it is permissible for her to return to the first husband if he desires that, and if they both know from themselves that they will uphold the limits of Allah between them by giving each one the rights of the other with good companionship. Otherwise, there is no return that is lawful for them. Therefore Allah said, *if they think that they will keep within the limits of Allah.* Then Allah exalted the matter of those limits, saying: ﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾, which are His laws, which He makes clear for a people who know, for those who know them are the ones who stop at them and do not transgress them, and so they are safe from the stain of injustice and the punishment of the unjust.

Lessons from the verse

1. A woman divorced three times is not lawful to her divorcer except under two conditions: first, that she marry another husband in a valid marriage, and that he consummate it with her and have intercourse with her; and second, that it be strongly presumed by each of them that the life between them will be good, and that the transgression that led to the divorce three times will not be repeated.

2. The death of the second husband is like his divorce; with it, return to the first husband is valid, under its condition.

3. If a divorced woman who has been divorced three times marries with the intention of defying her husband, so that he divorces her and she returns to the first, this marriage does not make her lawful for the first, for the sake of a legal device (taḥlīl), because the Messenger ﷺ nullified it and said: "Allah has cursed the muḥallil (one who makes lawful by a legal device) and the muḥallal lahu (the one for whom it is done)." He is called "the borrowed ram" (al-tays al-mustaʿār), the one who marries a woman divorced three times with the aim of making her lawful to the first husband.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 231:

Explanation of the words:

Ajalahunna (their term): the approaching of the end of the divorced woman's waiting period ('iddah).

Aw sarrihuhunna (or release them): releasing the divorced woman means leaving her without taking her back until her 'iddah ends and she becomes separated from her husband.

Dirar (harm): causing her harm and injuring her.

Li-ta'tadu (so that you transgress): so that you go beyond the limit of kindness into wrongdoing.

Huzuwan (in mockery): playing with them by not committing yourselves to applying their rulings.

Ni'mat Allah (the blessing of God): here it is Islam.

Al-hikmah (the wisdom): the Prophetic Sunnah.

Ya'izukum bihi (He admonishes you with it): with what He has sent down of rulings on the lawful and the unlawful, so that you may thank Him by obeying Him.

The meaning of the noble verse

The context continues to explain the rulings on divorce, khul' (divorce at the wife's request) and return (raj'ah) in this verse. God commands His believing servants, when one of them divorces his wife and her 'iddah is nearing its end, that he either take her back and keep her in ma'ruf (goodness), and ma'ruf is to treat her well in companionship, or leave her until her 'iddah ends and release her with ma'ruf, giving her all her full rights, mentioning her only with good, and letting her go wherever she wishes. He forbade one of them to take back his wife in order to harm her, neither treating her kindly nor divorcing her so that she may be relieved of him. So He said: ﴿And do not keep them, intending harm, so that you transgress﴾, meaning, keeping them so that the wronged woman is forced into khul' and ransoms herself from him with wealth. God informed that whoever commits this harm has exposed himself to the punishment of the Hereafter.

God also forbade the believers from toying with the legal rulings by neglecting them and not implementing them, so He said: ﴿And do not take the signs of God in mockery﴾. He commanded them to remember God's blessing upon them, as He favored them with Islam, the religion of mercy, justice and kindness, so that they would thank Him by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

They are also to remember God's blessing upon them in addition to Islam, which is the blessing of the sending down of the Book, and the wisdom, so that He admonishes them with it: He commands them with what brings their happiness and perfection, and forbids them from what brings their misery and loss. Then He commanded them to be mindful of Him, the Mighty and Majestic, saying ﴿And fear God﴾, and informed them that He is more worthy of being feared, because He is All-Knowing of everything, nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him, so let them beware that He sees them disobeying Him and turning away from His obedience.

Guidance of the verse

From the guidance of the verse:

1- It is not lawful for the divorcer to take back his wife in order to harm her and wrong her until she ransoms herself from him with wealth.

2- The prohibition of toying with the legal rulings by not observing and implementing them.

3- The obligation to mention God's blessing upon the servant, by mentioning it with the tongue and acknowledging it in the heart.

4- The obligation of fearing God, in secret and in public.

5- Being mindful of God in all aspects of life, for He is All-Knowing of everything.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 232:

Explanation of the words:

*Balaghna ajalahunna* (they have reached their term): meaning, their 'iddah (waiting period) has ended.

*Fa-la ta'dulluhunna* (do not prevent them): meaning, do not hinder them from marrying again by returning to the husband who divorced her and did not take her back until her 'iddah ended.

*Idha taradaw baynahum bil-ma'ruf* (when they agree between themselves in a reasonable manner): meaning, when the divorcing husband is content to take her back and she is content with that.

*Dhalika yu'a^zu bihi* (this is admonished with it): meaning, the prohibition of 'adl (obstruction) is enjoined upon the people of faith, for they are the ones capable of obedience.

*Dhalikum azka lakum* (that is purer for you): meaning, leaving obstruction is better for you than obstructing, and purer for your hearts, since obstruction may lead to committing immorality.

The meaning of the noble verse:

Allah the Exalted forbids the guardians of women from preventing a divorced woman, who has been divorced once or twice only, from returning to her husband who divorced her and from whom she became separated by the completion of her 'iddah, if she is content to marry him again and he is content with that, and they resolve to live together in a good manner, in accordance with what is reasonable. This verse was revealed in response to the sister of Ma'qil ibn Yasar (may Allah be pleased with him), when she wished to return to her husband who had divorced her and from whom she had separated upon the completion of the 'iddah, but her brother Ma'qil prevented her.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿This is admonished with it﴾, meaning: this prohibition of obstruction is directed to the people who believe in Allah and the Last Day, for they are the living who respond to Allah and His Messenger when they are commanded or forbidden.

Finally, Allah the Exalted informed them that not preventing the divorced woman from returning to her husband is better for them, in their present state and its outcome, and purer for their hearts and their community. He informed them that He knows the consequences of matters while they do not know, so it is obligatory to submit to accepting His law and to comply with His command and prohibition. Thus the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah knows, while you do not know﴾.

Guidance from the verse:

1- The prohibition of 'adl, i.e., preventing the divorced woman from returning to the one who divorced her.

2- The obligation of guardianship over the woman, because the address in the verse was to the guardians: "and do not prevent them."

3- Admonitions benefit the people of faith, because of the life of their hearts.

4- In carrying out the commands of Allah and avoiding His prohibitions lies all good and all purity.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 233:

Explanation of the words:

ḥawlayn: two years.

wa-ʿalā l-mawlūd lahu: that is, upon the father.

bil-maʿrūf: according to his circumstances, in wealth and in poverty.

wusʿahā: her capacity, and what she is able to bear.

lā tuḍārr wālidatun bi-waladihā: that is, it is not permissible to harm the mother of the child by preventing her from nursing her child, or by withholding from her the payment for nursing him, in the case of her divorce or the death of her husband.

wa-lā mawlūdun lahu: that is, nor is the father to be harmed likewise, by being compelled to have the child nursed by his divorced mother, or by being asked for a wage he cannot afford.

wa-ʿalā l-wārith: the heir is the infant himself if he has property; otherwise it falls upon whoever supports him from among his paternal relatives.

fiṣālan: weaning the child before the end of the two years.

The meaning of the noble verse:

In connection with explaining the rulings on divorce, since a woman may sometimes be divorced while pregnant, God Most High mentioned the rulings on nursing, and said: ﴿And mothers shall nurse their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾. That is, the divorced mother must nurse her child for two full years if she and the father of the infant wish to complete the nursing. And upon the one to whom the child belongs, who is the father, if he is present, is the obligation of providing for the nursing mother, with food, drink and clothing, according to what is customary, in accordance with the father's circumstances of wealth or poverty, since God does not burden a soul except with what He has given it of capacity.

Then God Most High warned that it is not permissible to harm the mother because of her child, by preventing her from nursing her child or by forcing her to nurse him when she does not want to, or by withholding maintenance in return for nursing, or by restricting her in it. Likewise it is not permissible to harm the one to whom the child belongs, who is the father, by compelling him to have his child nursed by his mother after he has divorced her, nor by demanding an exorbitant payment he cannot afford. And upon the heir, who is the infant himself if he has property. If he has no property, then upon his male paternal relatives, the nearest first and then the next nearest; that is, they bear the wage of nursing. If the child has no property and no paternal relatives, the mother is obliged to nurse him without pay, because she is the nearest of people to him.

Then God Most High mentioned two concessions regarding nursing. The first: if the two parents wish to wean the child before two years, they may do so after mutual consultation and consideration of the child's welfare in this early weaning. God Most High said: ﴿But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation, there is no blame upon them﴾. That is, there is no narrowing or hardship. The second: if the one to whom the child belongs wishes to seek a wet-nurse other than his mother for his child, he may do so provided the mother is content with it. God Most High said: ﴿And if you wish to seek a wet-nurse for your children, there is no blame upon you﴾, on condition that the agreed wage is paid in a customary manner, without overreaching or procrastination.

Finally, God admonished both the nursing mother and the one whose child is nursed to fear Him in observing these limits He has set for them, and informed them that He is Seeing of what they do, so let them beware of opposing His command and committing what He has forbidden. Glorified is He, a great God, Righteous and Merciful.

Guidance from the verse:

1- The obligation on the mother to nurse her child with the first milk (al-laba') if she is divorced, and the rest of the nursing if she is not divorced.

2- Clarification of the upper limit of nursing, which is two complete years. Therefore, anything beyond them is not legally recognized.

3- Permissibility of taking a wage for nursing.

4- The obligation of maintenance of relatives upon one another in cases of poverty.

5- Permissibility of the father having his child nursed by someone other than his mother.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 2, verses 234–235**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Yatawaffawna* (﻿يتوفون): Allah fulfills for them the lifespan He has decreed, so they die.

*Wa yadharuna azwajan* (ويذرون أزواجاً): they leave behind wives.

*Yatarabbasna bi-anfusihinna* (يتربصن بأنفسهن): they wait until the end of their *'iddah* (the prescribed waiting period), which is four months and ten nights.

*Balaghna ajalahunna* (بلغن أجلهن): they have reached the end of the *'iddah*.

*La junaha 'alaykum* (لا جناح عليكم): there is no blame upon you, O guardians, for what they do regarding themselves, such as applying perfume, adorning themselves, and allowing themselves to be approached for marriage.

*La junaha 'alaykum* (لا جناح عليكم): there is no sin upon you in making an allusion to the proposal rather than explicitly proposing, just as there is no sin in harboring a desire in one's heart.

*Hatta yablugha al-kitabu ajalahu* (حتى يبلغ الكتاب أجله): that is, until the *'iddah* ends.

**The meaning of the two verses:**

The context continues to explain the rulings on divorce, the waiting period, and maintenance. In this verse [234], a woman whose husband has died must wait four months and ten nights if she is free, or half of that period if she is a slave. During this time she must not adorn herself, must not apply perfume, and must not allow herself to be approached for marriage in any way, until the *'iddah* prescribed in the verse has ended. The exception is a pregnant woman, whose *'iddah* ends with the delivery of her child, as stated in Allah's words in Surah al-Talaq: ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾ [65:4]. When she has reached her term, that is, when the period in which she is required to observe mourning has ended, there is no blame upon the family of her deceased husband or upon her own family for what she does regarding herself, such as discontinuing the mourning (*ihdad*) and allowing herself to be approached for marriage. This is the meaning of Allah's words: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait for themselves four months and ten days. And when they have reached their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner﴾, meaning in what is permissible for them. He concludes the verse with an admonition: ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾, so beware of Him and do not do anything except what He has permitted you.

As for the second verse [235], it includes the prohibition of proposing marriage to a woman in her *'iddah*, whether from divorce or from the death of her husband. It is not lawful to propose to her, because such a proposal may cause harm. A man who is desirable for his wealth, religion, or lineage may lead the woman to claim that her waiting period has ended when it has not, and it may cause her husband who divorced her to lose the opportunity to take her back. All of this is forbidden harm. The verse also begins by lifting the blame for making an allusion to a proposal, short of an explicit forbidden statement. Allah says: ﴿And there is no blame upon you﴾, O Muslims, for what you allude to in proposing to women in their *'iddah*, such as saying: "I am interested in marriage," or: "When your waiting period ends, consult me if you wish to marry." The verse also reveals the state of the man's heart, as Allah says: ﴿Allah knows that you will remember them﴾, expressing your desire to marry them. So He permitted you to make allusions rather than explicit statements. But ﴿do not make promises to them in secret﴾. This phrase indicates the prohibition of proposing to a woman in her *'iddah* after death or after an irrevocable divorce. As for a revocable divorce, it is not valid to propose, either by allusion or explicitly, because she is in the status of a wife. His words ﴿except that you say a kind word﴾ mean permission for allusion.

This verse also includes the prohibition of concluding a marriage contract with a woman in her *'iddah* until her waiting period has ended. Allah says: ﴿And do not resolve upon the marriage contract until the decreed term has reached its end﴾. **Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 2, verses 234–235**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Yatawaffawna* (﻿يتوفون): Allah fulfills for them the lifespan He has decreed, so they die.

*Wa yadharuna azwajan* (ويذرون أزواجاً): they leave behind wives.

*Yatarabbasna bi-anfusihinna* (يتربصن بأنفسهن): they wait until the end of their *'iddah* (the prescribed waiting period), which is four months and ten nights.

*Balaghna ajalahunna* (بلغن أجلهن): they have reached the end of the *'iddah*.

*La junaha 'alaykum* (لا جناح عليكم): there is no blame upon you, O guardians, for what they do regarding themselves, such as applying perfume, adorning themselves, and allowing themselves to be approached for marriage.

*La junaha 'alaykum* (لا جناح عليكم): there is no sin upon you in making an allusion to the proposal rather than explicitly proposing, just as there is no sin in harboring a desire in one's heart.

The context continues to explain the rulings on divorce, the waiting period, and maintenance. During this time she must not adorn herself, must not apply perfume, and must not allow herself to be approached for marriage in any way, until the *'iddah* prescribed in the verse has ended. And when they have reached their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner﴾, meaning in what is permissible for them. He concludes the verse with an admonition: ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾, so beware of Him and do not do anything except what He has permitted you.

As for a revocable divorce, it is not valid to propose, either by allusion or explicitly, because she is in the status of a wife. His words ﴿except that you say a kind word﴾ mean permission for allusion.

This verse also includes the prohibition of concluding a marriage contract with a woman in her *'iddah* until her waiting period has ended. Allah says: ﴿And do not resolve upon the marriage contract until the decreed term has reached its end﴾. So they should beware of Him with the utmost caution and not oppose His command or His prohibition. He also informed them that He is Forgiving to those among them who repent after sin, and Forbearing toward them, not hastening punishment upon them so that they may have the opportunity to repent.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 236–239:

Explanation of the words:

al-Junah (blame): the sin that results from disobedience.

Ma lam tamassuhunna (as long as you have not touched them): as long as you have not had intercourse with them.

Aw tafridu (or you specify): you determine a dower (mahr) for them.

al-Muwassi' qadaruhu (the wealthy man according to his means): one who has ample wealth, and qadaruhu (his measure): what he is able to afford and is capable of.

al-Muqtir (the one of restricted means): one whose livelihood is straitened.

Alladhi biyadihi 'uqdat al-nikah (the one in whose hand is the tie of marriage): this is the husband.

Wa la tansawu al-fadl baynakum (and do not forget graciousness between you): that is, mutual affection and kindness.

Hafizu 'ala al-salawat (guard the prayers): by performing them at their proper times, in congregation, with fulfilment of their conditions, pillars and recommended practices.

As-Salat al-Wusta (the middle prayer): it is the Asr prayer, or the Fajr prayer. Thus it is obligatory to guard all the prayers, especially the Asr and the Fajr, due to the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Whoever prays the two cooler prayers (al-bardayn), Asr and Fajr, will enter Paradise." Qanitin (devoutly obedient): humble and still.

Rijalan (on foot): walking on your feet, or riding on animals and other things that are ridden.

The meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to explain the rulings of divorce and what relates to it. In this verse [236], Allah the Exalted informs His believing servants that there is no sin or blame upon them if they divorce their wives before consummating the marriage and before specifying dowers for them. In these two situations, they must provide the divorced woman, who has not been given a dower and for whom no dower was specified, with a provision, so that its amount is known in this case. It may be rare. The divorcing husband must, to console her, give her wealth according to his wealth and poverty, which she enjoys for some days in compensation for what she has missed of the enjoyment of marriage. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not yet touched them or specified for them an obligatory payment. But provide for them, the wealthy according to his capacity and the poor according to his capacity, a provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the doers of good.﴾

As for the second verse [237], Allah the Exalted informs that whoever divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, and has specified a dower for her, whether little or much, is obligated to give her half of it, unless the divorced woman forgoes it out of generosity, or the divorcing man forgoes it out of generosity, so he takes nothing from her and gives her all of it. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them but have already specified for them an obligatory payment, then half of what you specified﴾ – that is, the obligation is half of what you specified – ﴿unless they (the divorced women) forgo it, or he in whose hand is the tie of marriage (the husband) forgoes it.﴾ Then, after establishing this just and merciful ruling, Allah the Exalted called both parties to forgiveness, and that whoever of them forgives is nearer to piety. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And that you forgo is nearer to righteousness﴾, and He forbade them, along with this, from forgetting the affection and kindness between them, saying: ﴿And do not forget graciousness between you. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

As for the third verse [238], Allah the Exalted guides His believing servants to what helps them adhere to these obligatory duties and noble Islamic manners, which is guarding the establishment of the five daily prayers in general and the middle prayer in particular. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾. Before this, they used to speak during prayer, so He forbade them from that by His saying: ﴿And stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾, that is, still and humble.

If fear arises such that they cannot perform the prayer in the required manner of stillness and humility, then they should pray while walking on foot or riding on their horses. Once the fear has passed and security is achieved, they should pray in the manner in which they used to pray, with stillness, quiet and humility. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you fear, then on foot or riding. And when you are secure, remember Allah as He has taught you that which you did not know.﴾ By remembrance here, Allah the Exalted means establishing the prayer first, then general remembrance, reminding them of the blessing of knowledge and requiring them to thank Him for it, which is to perform the prayer in its most complete and perfect forms, because it is the aid to all other acts of obedience, and it is enough that it forbids indecency and wrongdoing. This is what the fourth verse [239] contains.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Explanation of the ruling on a woman divorced before consummation and before a dower is specified: she is entitled only to a provision, according to the divorcing husband's wealth or poverty.

2- Explanation of the ruling on a woman divorced before consummation for whom a dower was specified: she is obligated to receive half of it, unless she waives it willingly, in which case that is permitted for her; likewise, if the divorcing husband waives the half and gives her the full specified dower, that is permitted for him.

3- The call to preserve affection, graciousness and kindness between the two families, the family of the divorced woman and the family of the divorcing husband, so that divorce does not become a cause of enmity and estrangement.

4- The obligation to guard the five daily prayers, especially the Asr prayer and the Fajr prayer, "the middle prayer."

5- The prohibition of speaking during prayer except for its correction.

6- The obligation of humility (khushu') in prayer.

7- Explanation of the prayer of one who fears an enemy or other threat, and that it is permissible for him to pray while walking or riding.

8- The command to constantly remember Allah and to give thanks for His blessings, especially the blessing of knowledge of Islam.

2- Explanation of the ruling on a woman divorced before consummation for whom a dower was specified: she is obligated to receive half of it, unless she waives it willingly, in which case that is permitted for her; likewise, if the divorcing husband waives the half and gives her the full specified dower, that is permitted for him.

3- The call to preserve affection, graciousness and kindness between the two families, the family of the divorced woman and the family of the divorcing husband, so that divorce does not become a cause of enmity and estrangement.

4- The obligation to guard the five daily prayers, especially the Asr prayer and the Fajr prayer, "the middle prayer."

5- The prohibition of speaking during prayer except for its correction.

6- The obligation of humility (khushu') in prayer.

7- Explanation of the prayer of one who fears an enemy or other threat, and that it is permissible for him to pray while walking or riding.

8- The command to constantly remember Allah and to give thanks for His blessings, especially the blessing of knowledge of Islam.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 240–242:

Explanation of the words:

Al-hawl (الحول): the year.

Fa-in kharajna (فإن خرجن): i.e., leave the house of the deceased husband before the year is over.

Matā'an bil-ma'rūf (متاع بالمعروف): i.e., a provision without excess, and without shortfall.

Haqqan (حقاً): an obligation incumbent upon the righteous divorcing men.

The meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues to explain the rights of divorced women and of widows. In this verse [240], God the Exalted informs that those among the believers who die and leave wives, then for them there is a bequest from God the Exalted upon the heirs of the deceased husband to carry out: that they permit the widow to remain with them in the house, eating and drinking, until the end of the year, including the period of the waiting term ('iddah), which is four months and ten nights, unless she wishes to leave after the waiting term has ended, in which case that is permitted for her. This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind—they shall bequeath to their wives a provision for a year without being turned out. But if they leave, then there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves, within what is reasonable. And Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾ His saying "then there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves" has already been explained in meaning, namely that the woman observing the waiting term, once her waiting term has ended, may adorn herself, use perfume, and make herself available for proposals in order to marry. And the verse concluding with "And Allah is Mighty and Wise" indicates that this bequest was legislated by the Mighty, the Wise, so it is binding in its realisation and implementation.

As for the second verse [241]: ﴿And for divorced women is a provision in kindness, as an obligation upon the righteous.﴾ In it there is another ruling: that a divorced woman with whom the marriage was consummated should be provided by her former husband with something of wealth, such as garments, a riding animal, or a servant. Accordingly, a divorced woman before consummation for whom a dower was specified receives only half the dower and nothing else; and the provision (mut'ah) for a divorced woman before consummation for whom no dower was specified is obligatory for her, since she has nothing other than it. The divorced woman after consummation, who is the one intended in this verse, has a provision in kindness, whether it is said to be obligatory or recommended, because she is owed the full dower.

And His saying, the Exalted, in the third verse [242]: ﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses, that you may understand.﴾ Its meaning: just as this clarification of the rulings on divorce, khul', breastfeeding, the waiting terms, and provisions, Allah the Exalted clarifies to us His verses containing the rulings of His legislation, so that we may understand them, act upon them, be perfected by them, and be happy in both the present life and the Hereafter.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Permitting a widow observing the waiting term to remain in the house of the deceased for a year, if her soul is content with that, and this is after the obligatory waiting term has ended; the excess, which is seven months and twenty days, was enjoined in this bequest. However, the majority of scholars say that this bequest has been abrogated (naskh), and not saying that there is abrogation is preferable, because of their disagreement over what abrogates it.

2- The right of a divorced woman with whom the marriage was consummated to a provision in kindness.

3- God's favour upon this community in clarifying the rulings for it, so that it may be happy by them and be perfected by them; so to God belong praise and thanks.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 243–245:

Explanation of the words:

*Alam tara* (ألم تر): "Has it not reached your knowledge..." So the seeing is of the heart, and the interrogation is for wonder.

*Alf* (ألوف): the plural of *alf* (thousand), a form indicating multiplicity, so it means tens of thousands.

*Fi sabil Allah* (في سبيل الله): the path that leads to His good pleasure, which is obedience by carrying out His command and avoiding His prohibition, and among that is fighting the disbelievers and the wrongdoers so that there is no fitnah.

*Yuqridu Allah* (يقرض الله): sets aside a portion of his wealth and spends it in jihad, for buying weapons and equipping the mujahidin.

*Yaqbid wa yabsut* (يقبض ويبسط): "He constricts and expands"; He constricts as a trial and expands as a test.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah the Exalted addresses His Messenger ﷺ, saying: "Has the story not reached your knowledge of those who went out of their homes fleeing death, while they were thousands? They were the people of a city of the Children of Israel, on whom Allah sent the plague, so they fled from death, and Allah caused them to die to the last of them. Then He brought them back to life through the supplication of their prophet Ezekiel (Hizqil), peace be upon him." Did their flight save them from death? Likewise, does the one who flees from fighting save himself from death by his flight? The answer is no. So why flee from jihad when it becomes obligatory? In the chastisement of that group by causing them to die and then reviving them, there is a great favour from Allah upon them, but most people do not give thanks. So fight, O Muslims, in the path of Allah, and do not hold back whenever you are called to jihad with your lives and wealth, and know that Allah is All-Hearing of your words and All-Knowing of your intentions and deeds, so beware of Him. Then the Exalted opened the door of financial contribution to jihad, saying: "Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan" with no admixture of shirk toward anyone, and with a willing soul, for Allah multiplies it for him many times over, a dirham becoming seven hundred dirhams. So spend, O believers, for the elevation of the word of Allah, and do not fear poverty, for your Lord "constricts and expands": He constricts upon the servant as a trial and expands as a test. Your withholding from spending in the path of Allah changes nothing of Allah's arrangement.

Guidance from the verses:

1- When plague descends upon a land, it is not permissible to leave it fleeing from it; this is established by the Sunnah.

2- The obligation of remembering blessings and giving thanks for them.

3- The obligation of fighting in the path of Allah when it becomes obligatory (fard 'ayn).

4- The virtue of spending in the path of Allah.

5- Explanation of the wisdom in Allah's constricting and expanding a servant's provision: constriction is a trial that calls for patience, and expansion is a test that calls for gratitude. How disappointed is the one who does not endure patiently when provision is constricted for him, and does not give thanks when it is expanded for him.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 2, Verses 246–247**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Al-Mala'* (the notables): the leading people among those who have authority to bind and loosen, that is, to decide affairs. When a person looks at them, they fill his eye with splendour and his heart with awe.

*'Asa* (perhaps): a word expressing expectation and hope.

*Kutiba* (was prescribed): was made obligatory and required.

*Malikan* (a king): one who governs them in peace and in war.

*Anna yakunu* (how can he be?): the interrogative is used for denial, meaning how can kingship belong to him.

*Istafahu* (chose him): preferred him over you and selected him for you.

*Bastatan fi al-jism* (abundance in stature): an increase in height by which he rises above others.

**The meaning of the verses:**

Allah the Exalted had prescribed fighting upon the believers, and the wheels of battle turned, beginning with the Battle of Badr. Wealth and brave, courageous men were necessary. This situation required sharpening resolve and stirring feelings, so that the Muslim community in Madinah would be strong enough to face the war of the Arabs and the non-Arabs together. Here, in order to pursue cowardice and miserliness, which are among the worst qualities in men, Allah the Exalted mentioned the incident of those who fled from death, leaving their homes to others: how Allah caused them to die, and their flight did not save them. Then He brought them back to life so that this would be a lesson for them and for others. Fleeing from death is of no benefit; what benefits is patience and steadfastness until victory.

Then Allah commanded the believers, after this scene had taken its effect on their souls, saying: ﴿And fight in the way of Allah, and know that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 190, 244]. Since wealth is needed for fighting, Allah opened for them a financial appeal and multiplied the reward for a loan, on condition that it be sincere and given with a willing soul. Then He presented to them this detailed account of another incident, which bears within it admonitions and lessons for those who are in the position of the Muslims, who are fought by the white and the red alike, without respite and over a long span of time. Allah said, addressing them through the person of their Prophet (ﷺ):

﴿Have you not considered the notables of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs, "Appoint for us a king, that we may fight in the way of Allah"?﴾ He means: has it not reached your knowledge, through our informing you, that the notables of the Children of Israel, after the death of Moses, said to a prophet among them: "Raise up for us a king, so that we may fight in the way of Allah, drive out our enemies from our lands, regain our sovereignty, and establish the law of our Lord."

Because of their spiritual, physical and financial weakness, the Prophet feared that they would not be sincere in what they asked for. So he said: ﴿Is it likely that if fighting is prescribed for you, you will not fight?﴾, meaning, once the king-commander is appointed, that you will not fight? Then zeal drove them, and they said: "Why should we not fight in the way of Allah, when we have been driven out of our homes and from our children?" This was because the enemy, namely the Babylonians, invaded Palestine after the Children of Israel had become corrupt. Their women displayed themselves immodestly, they made adultery and usury lawful, they neglected the Scripture, and they turned away from the guidance of their prophets. So Allah gave this mighty enemy power over them, and he scattered them, and they became refugees.

The Prophet of Allah, Shmuel (Samuel), did what he did: he raised up from those dead communities, dead in a spiritual sense, a man from among them, Talut (Saul), and he led them. When they drew near to the battle, they lost their nerve, and most of them turned back in defeat before the fighting began. Their Prophet had been right in his insight when he said to them: ﴿Is it likely that if fighting is prescribed for you, you will not fight?﴾

This is what the first verse [246] of this story contains. As for the second verse [247], it contains the objection of the notables of the Children of Israel to the appointment of Talut as king over them, on the pretext that he is poor and from a family that is not noble, and that they have more right to this position than he does. Their Prophet answered their false argument by saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him broadly in knowledge and physique. And Allah gives His kingdom to whom He wills. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ This was Shmuel's reply to the words of the notables: ﴿How can he have kingship over us, when we are more worthy of kingship than he, and he has not been given abundance of wealth?﴾

It is as if, when the proof overwhelmed them, namely that Allah the Exalted had chosen Talut and preferred him over them by this choice, and made him fit for authority by what He had given him and increased in him of knowledge and physical strength, while military leadership depends on abundant knowledge and physical strength, with sound senses and the courage of mind and heart, I say: it is as if, when their objection was refuted and they accepted Talut, they demanded, in keeping with the habit of the Children of Israel in obstinacy, a sign showing that Allah had truly chosen him to lead them. So he said to them, etc., and this is the verse [248] that follows.

And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ This was Shmuel's reply to the words of the notables: ﴿How can he have kingship over us, when we are more worthy of kingship than he, and he has not been given abundance of wealth?﴾

It is as if, when the proof overwhelmed them, namely that Allah the Exalted had chosen Talut and preferred him over them by this choice, and made him fit for authority by what He had given him and increased in him of knowledge and physical strength, while military leadership depends on abundant knowledge and physical strength, with sound senses and the courage of mind and heart, I say: it is as if, when their objection was refuted and they accepted Talut, they demanded, in keeping with the habit of the Children of Israel in obstinacy, a sign showing that Allah had truly chosen him to lead them. So he said to them, etc., and this is the verse [248] that follows.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 248:

Explanation of the words:

Nabiyyahum (their prophet): Shamwil (Samuel).

Aayat mulkihi (the sign of his kingship): a sign that Allah the Exalted has made him king over you.

At-tabut (the ark): a wooden chest containing remnants of the relics of the family of Musa and the family of Harun.

Sakinah (tranquillity): the calm of the heart and the peace of the soul.

Baqiyyah (remnant): the remainder of a thing after most of it has gone. Here it refers to fragments of the tablets that were broken, Musa's staff, and some relics of their prophets.

Tahmiluhu al-mala'ikah (carried by the angels): from the land of the Amalekites, placing it before the Children of Israel in their camps.

Inna fi dhalika la-ayatan lakum (indeed, in that is a sign for you): that is, in the return to you of the ark, which the enemy had taken from you by force, is a strong sign of Allah the Exalted's choice of Talut as king over you.

The meaning of the noble verse:

Now that the explanation of the words has made the meaning of the verse clear, its summary is that the prophet Shamwil informed them that the sign of Allah the Exalted's appointing Talut over them is that the ark, which had been seized from them, would come to them. It was a symbol of their unity and cohesion, and a source from which their morale drew strength, because of what it contained of the relics of the family of Musa and the family of Harun, such as the fragments of the tablets, Musa's staff, his sandal, Harun's turban, and some of the manna that used to descend upon them in the wilderness. So this ark served as a banner under which they fought: when they went out to battle they carried it with them into the midst of the fight, and they would keep fighting as long as the ark remained in their hands, never having been overcome by their enemy while it was with them. Hence, as they prepared themselves for battle, Allah the Exalted made the coming of the ark a sign of Talut's appointment as king over them, and at the same time they would carry it with them in their fighting, so their hearts would be tranquil and their souls calm, and they would fight and be victorious by the permission of Allah the Exalted.

(As for how the angels carried the ark: the reports say that the Amalekites regarded the ark among them as a bad omen when they were afflicted with haemorrhoids and crop diseases and other calamities. They thought of returning this ark to the Children of Israel, and Allah brought about one circumstance after another, so they placed it in a cart drawn by two cows or two horses and directed it toward the dwellings of the Children of Israel. The cart moved, and the angels drove it until they brought it to the dwellings of the Children of Israel.) It was a sign, and a great sign, and the Children of Israel accepted Talut as their leader, and under the name of Allah the Exalted he led them. The following verse [249] explains the march to the battlefields.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 249:

Explanation of the words:

Fasala Talut (فصل طالوت): he departed from the homeland and set out intending the enemy.

Bil-junud (بالجنود): the army and its number, as it is said: seventy thousand fighters.

Mubtalikum binahr (مبتليكم بنهر): testing you with a flowing river, which is perhaps the River Jordan now.

Wa man lam yat'amhu (ومن لم يطعمه): whoever does not drink from it.

Ghurfa (غرفة): ghurfa with a fatha is the single instance, and with a damma is the noun from scooping (ightirāf).

Alladhina amanu ma'ahu (الذين آمنوا معه): they are those who did not drink from the river; as for whoever drank, he has disbelieved and committed shirk.

Annahum mulaqu Allah (أنهم مُلاقوُ اللَّهِ): that is, on the Day of Resurrection, for they believe in the Final Resurrection.

Kam min fi'a (كم من فئة): kam is for multiplication, and al-fi'a is the group, some of which returns to others.

Wallahu ma'a as-sabirin (والله مع الصابرين): He keeps them firm, helps them, and grants them victory.

The meaning of the verse:

When Talut set out with the army, he informed them that Allah the Exalted was testing them on their march to fight their enemy by means of a river they would reach while in intense heat and intense thirst. He did not permit them to drink from it except a single scoop. Whoever obeyed and did not drink is the believer, and whoever disobeyed and drank what was not permitted is the disbeliever. When they reached the river, they drank from it greedily like cattle, except for a few of them. Talut continued the march, crossing the river together with those who were with him. When they were near the enemy army, which numbered about one hundred thousand, the disbelievers and hypocrites said: ﴿We have no strength today against Jalut and his soldiers﴾, so they declared their defeat, turned back and fled. But the sincere believers, who are the ones Allah described when He said ﴿Those who were certain that they would meet Allah said: "How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah! And Allah is with the patient."﴾ said this. This verse explains Talut's march toward the enemy, and in the two following verses [250] and [251] is the explanation of the battle and its outcome, a decisive victory for the sincere believers. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when they came out against Jalut and his soldiers, they said: "Our Lord, pour upon us patience and make firm our feet..."﴾.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 250–252:

Explanation of the words:

Barazu li-Jalut (برزوا لجالوت): they appeared on the field of battle; Jalut (Goliath) was the commander of the forces of the Amalekites (al-'Amaliqa).

Afrigh 'alayna sabran (أفرغ علينا صبرا): pour patience upon us in abundance, until our hearts are filled with it, so that there is no room left for fear and anxiety.

Wa thabbit aqdamana (وثبت أقدامنا): in the land of battle, so that we do not flee; this is by strengthening our hearts and firming up our resolve.

Dawud (داود): the Prophet of Allah and His Messenger, Dawud (David). At that time he was neither a prophet nor a messenger, being in the army of Talut (Saul).

Wa atahu Allahu al-mulk wa al-hikmah (وآتاه الله الملك والحكمة): this took place after the death of the Prophet Shamwil (Samuel) and the death of King Talut.

Wa 'allamahu mimma yasha' (وعلَّمه مما يشاء): He taught him the craft of making armor, and the understanding of the speech of birds; he and his son Sulayman, peace be upon them both.

Lafasadati al-ard (لفسدت الأرض): this refers to the domination of the people of polytheism over the people of monotheism, and of the people of disbelief over the people of faith.

Meaning of the verses:

When the two armies met, the army of faith and the army of disbelief, Jalut challenged to single combat. Dawud came out to him from the army of Talut and killed him, and the two armies closed in combat. Allah granted victory to the army of Talut, whose number was three hundred and fourteen fighters and no more, in accordance with the saying of the Messenger ﷺ to the people of Badr: "You are on the number of the companions of Talut," and they were three hundred and fourteen men. Allah defeated the army of falsehood despite its multitude and gave victory to the army of truth despite its scarcity. Here the star of Dawud appeared on the horizon by his killing the head of evil, Jalut, and Allah honoured him with prophethood and kingship after the death of both the Prophet Shamwil and the King Talut. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Dawud killed Jalut, and Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom and taught him from what He willed﴾.

Allah concluded the story, rich in lessons and great admonitions, with His saying: ﴿And were it not that Allah checks one set of people by means of another﴾ through jihad and fighting. Otherwise the people of disbelief would have overpowered and corrupted the earth with oppression, polytheism and sins. But Allah, by His wise design, lets some dominate others and repels some by others, as a favour and bounty from Him. As He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿But Allah is full of bounty to the worlds﴾.

Then He turned to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ and said to him, affirming his prophethood and the loftiness of his station: ﴿These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers﴾ ﷺ.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Lawful jihad requires an imam who has received a lawful pledge of allegiance (bay'ah).

2- Authority requires competence, the most important qualities of which are knowledge and soundness of mind and body.

3- It is permissible to seek blessing through the relics of the prophets, such as the turban, garment or sandal of the Prophet, for example.

4- It is permissible to test the members of an army to know the extent of their readiness for fighting and their endurance of it.

5- The excellence of faith in meeting Allah, and the excellence of patience in obeying Allah, especially in the battles of jihad in the way of Allah.

6- Clarification of the wisdom behind the legislation of jihad, which is repelling the people of disbelief and oppression with the people of faith and justice, so that life may be organized and the universe flourish.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 253–254:

Explanation of the words:

Those messengers (تلك الرسل): those messengers whom God Most High related to His Messenger some of them, and informed him that he was among them, in His saying ﴿And indeed, you are among the messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 252], in the verse before this one.

Whom God spoke to (من كَلَّم الله): such as Moses, peace be upon him.

And raised some of them in degrees (ورفع بعضهم درجات): this is Muhammad (ﷺ), as He preferred him with a distinguished preference over all the other messengers.

The clear proofs (البينات): the miracles that indicate the truthfulness of Jesus in his prophethood and messengership.

The Holy Spirit (روح القدس): Gabriel, peace be upon him, who was always standing beside Jesus, supporting and strengthening him until God Most High raised him up to Himself.

They fought (اقتتلوا): some of them killed others.

Spend from what We have provided for you (أنفقوا مما رزقناكم): the obligatory spending, which is zakat, and voluntary recommended spending.

No trading (لا بيع فيه): no one can buy himself back with wealth that he gives as a ransom for himself from the punishment.

Nor friendship (ولا خُلة): meaning friendship that benefits its companion.

Nor intercession (ولا شَفاعة): accepted, except by God's permission for whom He wills and is pleased with.

And the disbelievers (والكافرون): by withholding zakat and the obligatory rights owed to God Most High and to His servants, they are the wrongdoers.

The meaning of the two verses:

After God, blessed and exalted, related to His Messenger the story of the chiefs of the Children of Israel in their request of their prophet Shamwil that he appoint for them a king who would lead them to jihad. The story contained within its folds events that someone unlettered like Muhammad (ﷺ) could not have known without receiving them as a revelation that God revealed to him. He concluded the story by affirming his prophethood and messengership with His saying: ﴿And indeed, you are among the messengers﴾. God, Most High, informed that these messengers were preferred over one another: among them is one whom He preferred by speaking to him, such as Moses, peace be upon him; among them is one whom He preferred by friendship, such as Abraham, peace be upon him; among them is one whom He raised up to Himself, brought near, and conversed with privately, and he is Muhammad (ﷺ); among them is one to whom He gave kingship and wisdom and taught him the craft of armor, such as David, peace be upon him; among them is one to whom He gave kingship and wisdom, subjected the jinn to him and taught him the speech of birds, such as Solomon, peace be upon him; and among them is one to whom He gave clear proofs and supported with the Holy Spirit, and he is Jesus, peace be upon him. So God, Most High, said: ﴿Those messengers — We preferred some of them over others; among them are those whom God spoke to, and some of them He raised in degrees﴾, meaning our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), when He preferred him by the universality of his messengership, by sealing the prophethoods with his prophethood, by the preference of his nation, by admitting him to Paradise during his life before his death, by speaking to him and conversing with him, along with what He specially granted him of intercession on the Day of Resurrection. Then God, Most High, informed that if He willed to guide people, He would have guided them, so they would not have differed after their messengers, nor fought one another after the clear proofs had come to them; and that is due to His great power and the freedom of His will, for He does what He wills and decides what He desires. This is some of what the first verse [253] conveyed. As for the second verse [254], God Most High called out to His believing servants and commanded them to spend in the way of God, seeking nearness to Him and provision for meeting Him before the Day of Resurrection, when there is no ransom by sale or purchase, no friendship that benefits, and no intercession that avails. The disbelievers in God's blessings and laws are the wrongdoers, deserving punishment, deprivation and loss.

Guidance from the two verses:

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The messengers differ in preference among themselves according to their jihad, their patience, and the perfection God Most High granted them.

2- The attribute of speech for God Most High, as He spoke to Moses at Mount Sinai and spoke to Muhammad in the Highest Kingdom.

3- Disbelief and faith, guidance and misguidance, war and peace — all of this follows His Most High will and wisdom.

4- The blameworthiness of disagreement in religion, and that it is a source of misery and punishment.

5- The obligation of spending in the way of God from what God Most High has provided to His servant.

6- A warning against heedlessness and taking the means of salvation on the Day of Resurrection, when there is no ransom, no friendship that benefits, and no intercession; and among the strongest means are faith, righteous deeds, and spending wealth seeking nearness to God Most High, in jihad and otherwise.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verse 255:

Explanation of the words:

Allah: a proper name (ʿalam) for the Essence of the Lord, blessed and exalted.

Lā ilāha illā Huwa: al-Ilah (the one worshipped, al-maʿbud). None is worthy of worship in truth except Allah, for He is the Creator, the Provider, who manages everything by His hand, and to whom the outcome of all things returns. Whatever else is taken as a deity, its worship is without right and is false.

Al-Hayy: the One possessed of a great life, which is not possessed by anyone other than Him, exalted is He, and which entails power, will, knowledge, hearing, sight, and speech.

Al-Qayyum: the One who sustains the management of the entire dominion, the higher and the lower, and who stands over every soul for what it has earned.

As-Sinah: drowsiness, which precedes sleep.

Kursiyyuhu: the Kursi is the place of the feet, and none knows its reality except Allah, exalted is He.

Yaʾuduhu: burdens Him and is difficult for Him.

Meaning of the noble verse:

When Allah, exalted is He, informed about the Day of Resurrection, that it is a day on which there is no trade and no intercession, and that the disbelievers are the wrongdoers, He informed about His majesty, His perfection, and the greatness of His sovereignty, and that He is the One worthy of worship in truth, and that worshipping Him is what saves from the terrors of the Day of Resurrection. So He said: ﴿Allah! There is no god but Him﴾: that is, He is Allah, the One worthy of worship in truth, and there is no one worthy of worship in truth besides Him. ﴿The Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾: the One whose life is everlasting, not preceded by death and not overtaken by death. Al-Qayyum: the Great One who sustains everything. Were it not for His sustaining of the creatures, nothing in the affairs of the worlds would be set right. ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾: for drowsiness and sleep are attributes of deficiency, and He, exalted is He, possesses absolute perfection. This sentence is a proof for the sentence before it, for one who becomes drowsy and sleeps cannot be the sustainer of the creatures, nor can he encompass them in preservation, provision, and management. ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾: in creation, ownership, and disposal. ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾: Allah, exalted is He, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, negates that anyone, whoever he may be, can intercede with Him, in this world or in the Hereafter, without His permitting him to intercede. ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾: because of the completeness of their incapacity. ﴿His Kursi encompasses the heavens and the earth﴾: because of the completeness of His Essence. ﴿And their preservation does not burden Him﴾: the preservation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them and between them does not burden Him or make Him labor. ﴿And He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾: the Most High, above whom there is nothing, the Subduer who cannot be overcome by anything, the Most Great before whose greatness everything is small and insignificant.

Guidance from the noble verse:

From the guidance of this verse:

1. It is the greatest verse in the Book of Allah, exalted is He. It contains eighteen names of Allah, exalted is He, some explicit and some implicit. Its words are fifty and its sentences are ten, all of them speaking of His lordship, His divinity, and His names and attributes, which indicate the perfection of His Essence, His knowledge, His power, and the greatness of His sovereignty.

2. It is recommended to recite it after the obligatory prayer, at the time of sleep, and in the houses to drive away Satan.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 2, verses 256–257:

Explanation of the words:

﴿لا إكراه في الدين﴾: a person is not compelled to enter the religion; rather, he embraces it by his own will and choice.

﴿الرشد﴾ (guidance): the guidance that leads to felicity and perfection.

﴿الغي﴾ (error): the misguidance that leads the servant to wretchedness and loss.

﴿الطاغوت﴾ (taghut): everything that turns one away from worshipping God, be it a human, a devil, or something else.

﴿العروة الوثقى﴾ (the firmest handhold): "There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God."

﴿لا انفصام لها﴾: it never breaks or dissolves under any circumstances.

﴿الله ولي الذين آمنوا﴾: its protector (mutawalli) for them, by His preservation, His support, and His granting of success.

﴿الظلمات﴾: the darkness of ignorance and disbelief.

﴿النور﴾: the light of faith and knowledge.

﴿أولياؤهم الطاغوت﴾: their protectors are the devils who made the worship of idols attractive to them, thus removing them from faith to disbelief and from knowledge to ignorance.

The meaning of the two verses:

God, after mentioning the attributes of His majesty and perfection in the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi), informs that there is no compulsion in His religion. This was when some of the Ansar wished to compel those of their children who had become Jews or Christians to enter the religion of Islam. Accordingly, the People of the Two Scriptures and those who resemble them are required to pay the jizya and are allowed to remain upon their religion; they do not leave it except by their own choice and free will. As for the idolaters and those who have no religion other than polytheism and disbelief, they are to be fought until they enter Islam, in order to rescue them from ignorance and disbelief and the misguidance and wretchedness that accompany them.

Then God informs that by sending down His Book, sending His Messenger, and giving victory to His friends, guidance has been made clear from error, and truth from falsehood. Accordingly, whoever disbelieves in the tyrant (taghut), who is the devil that made the worship of idols attractive, and believes in God, testifying that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, has grasped the firmest and most secure handhold of religion. Whoever persists in disbelief in God and belief in the tyrant has grasped at something weaker than a spider's thread. God is All-Hearing of the words of His servants and All-Knowing of their intentions and the hidden aspects of their deeds, and He will recompense each soul according to what it has earned. Then God informs that He is the Protector of His believing servants: He brings them out of the darkness of disbelief and ignorance into the light of knowledge and faith, so they are perfected and made happy; and that the disbelievers have as their protectors the tyrants of the jinn and mankind, the devils who made falsehood and evils seem good to them, and adorned for them disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience. Thereby they drew them out of the light into the darkness, and so made them fit for the Fire, and they became its companions, abiding in it forever.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The People of the Two Scriptures and those in their category, such as the Magians and the Sabians, are not compelled to enter Islam except by their own choice, and the jizya is accepted from them, and they are allowed to remain upon their religion.

2- All of Islam is guidance, and whatever is other than it is error and falsehood.

3- Abandoning vices takes precedence over adorning oneself with virtues.

4- The meaning of "There is no god but God," which is faith in God and disbelief in the tyrant.

5- The friendship of God is attained through faith and piety.

6- The support of God and His care for His friends, not for His enemies.
